papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Paradigm for Efficient and Adaptable Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient counterparts. This process, where a compact "student" model learns from a larger "teacher" model, is crucial for deploying state-of-the-art neural networks on resource-constrained devices. Beyond simple compression, distillation has evolved into a versatile framework for transferring knowledge in a variety of challenging contexts. It enables training without access to original data, facilitates collaborative learning across heterogeneous devices in federated settings, and improves model generalization and adaptation to new domains. This demonstrates that knowledge distillation is not merely a compression tool but a fundamental paradigm for making advanced artificial intelligence more practical, private, and widely applicable.

papers_seen.author: Anderson

papers_seen.author: Jones

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile model compression technique in deep learning that operates on a teacher-student paradigm. It involves training a smaller, more efficient student model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to create compact models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. This is achieved by transferring the rich knowledge from the teacher's soft probability outputs or intermediate feature representations to the student. The technique has widespread applications in fields such as natural language processing and computer vision. The framework has evolved to include advanced methods like multi-teacher, online, and self-distillation, as well as data-free approaches for scenarios with privacy constraints. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation is also leveraged to enhance model performance and improve learning robustness.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique in deep learning for compressing large, cumbersome models into smaller, more efficient counterparts. This teacher-student learning paradigm involves training a compact student model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary goal is to transfer the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, including nuanced relationships between classes, to the student, enabling it to achieve comparable or even superior performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost. This approach has proven effective across a wide range of applications, including natural language processing and computer vision, facilitating the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices and in specialized environments like federated learning. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation also serves as a potent regularization technique and a method for enhancing model performance and enabling novel cross-modal knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: SEED: Self-supervised Distillation For Visual Representation
papers_seen.abstract: This paper is concerned with self-supervised learning for small models. The problem is motivated by our empirical studies that while the widely used contrastive self-supervised learning method has shown great progress on large model training, it does not work well for small models. To address this problem, we propose a new learning paradigm, named SElf-SupErvised Distillation (SEED), where we leverage a larger network (as Teacher) to transfer its representational knowledge into a smaller architecture (as Student) in a self-supervised fashion. Instead of directly learning from unlabeled data, we train a student encoder to mimic the similarity score distribution inferred by a teacher over a set of instances. We show that SEED dramatically boosts the performance of small networks on downstream tasks. Compared with self-supervised baselines, SEED improves the top-1 accuracy from 42.2% to 67.6% on EfficientNet-B0 and from 36.3% to 68.2% on MobileNet-v3-Large on the ImageNet-1k dataset.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique used to create smaller, more efficient deep learning models without significant performance loss. The process involves transferring knowledge from a large, pre-trained "teacher" model to a more compact "student" model. This paradigm has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning. By leveraging the rich representations learned by the teacher, the student model can achieve high accuracy while being suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices or in latency-sensitive applications. This method proves versatile, addressing challenges such as domain adaptation, few-shot learning, and privacy-preserving federated learning.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: DINE: Domain Adaptation from Single and Multiple Black-box Predictors
papers_seen.abstract: To ease the burden of labeling, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to transfer knowledge in previous and related labeled datasets (sources) to a new unlabeled dataset (target). Despite impressive progress, prior methods always need to access the raw source data and develop data-dependent alignment approaches to recognize the target samples in a transductive learning manner, which may raise privacy concerns from source individuals. Several recent studies resort to an alternative solution by exploiting the well-trained white-box model from the source domain, yet, it may still leak the raw data through generative adversarial learning. This paper studies a practical and interesting setting for UDA, where only black-box source models (i.e., only network predictions are available) are provided during adaptation in the target domain. To solve this problem, we propose a new two-step knowledge adaptation framework called DIstill and fine-tuNE (DINE). Taking into consideration the target data structure, DINE first distills the knowledge from the source predictor to a customized target model, then fine-tunes the distilled model to further fit the target domain. Besides, neural networks are not required to be identical across domains in DINE, even allowing effective adaptation on a low-resource device. Empirical results on three UDA scenarios (i.e., single-source, multi-source, and partial-set) confirm that DINE achieves highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art data-dependent approaches. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/tim-learn/DINE/}.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression, Enhancement, and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning, primarily known for model compression. This method involves training a compact "student" model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. While its main application is to create smaller, faster models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, its utility extends far beyond this initial purpose. Knowledge distillation has been successfully adapted to enhance model performance, sometimes enabling student models to surpass their teachers. Furthermore, it serves as a crucial tool for addressing important practical and ethical considerations, including improving model robustness against adversarial attacks, ensuring algorithmic fairness, preserving data privacy, and increasing model interpretability. Its flexibility allows it to be applied across diverse domains such as natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, making it a multifaceted and indispensable technique in the modern machine learning toolkit.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique for compressing large deep learning models. This method involves training a smaller, computationally efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the nuanced 'dark knowledge' from the teacher's predictions, rather than just learning from ground-truth labels, the student model can achieve performance comparable to its larger counterpart while being significantly smaller and faster. This approach has proven effective across a wide range of applications, including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices without a substantial sacrifice in accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning and natural language processing. It involves a teacher-student framework where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to transfer the rich knowledge from the complex teacher to the compact student, thereby reducing computational and storage requirements without a significant loss in performance. This allows for the deployment of powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. The process can involve transferring knowledge from the teacher's final predictions, intermediate feature representations, or attention mechanisms, and has been successfully applied across various domains, including language modeling, machine translation, and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression technique that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient neural networks. This is achieved through a teacher-student framework, where a smaller "student" model is trained to replicate the outputs or internal representations of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. The primary goal is often to reduce the computational and memory footprint of state-of-the-art models, making them suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has also been shown to improve the performance of student models, sometimes enabling them to outperform models of a similar size trained from scratch. The technique has been successfully applied across a wide array of domains, including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph-based learning, with various methodological innovations continually expanding its utility.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing complexity of deep learning models has created significant challenges for their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible model compression technique to address this issue. This method involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model, effectively transferring its learned knowledge. This process enables the creation of smaller, faster models that retain high performance, making them suitable for practical applications. The versatility of knowledge distillation is demonstrated by its successful application across diverse domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning, as well as in specialized contexts like data-free learning and enhancing model interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique in deep learning, primarily known for model compression. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, cumbersome 'teacher' model, making it feasible to deploy state-of-the-art architectures on resource-constrained devices. However, the applications of knowledge distillation extend far beyond mere compression. It serves as a flexible framework for transferring knowledge to enhance model accuracy, enable continuous learning across sequential tasks, facilitate domain adaptation without source data, and even improve performance in multi-task learning settings. This versatility makes knowledge distillation a critical tool for advancing the practical application and capabilities of modern neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent technique for model compression in deep learning. This approach facilitates the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more computationally efficient model, the 'student'. The primary goal is to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. This teacher-student learning framework is not limited to simple label matching; it often involves transferring knowledge from intermediate layers and output distributions. The technique has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing for compressing large language models like BERT, and in computer vision for tasks such as object detection and image segmentation. Research has also explored advanced strategies like data-free distillation to address privacy concerns and methods to train more effective 'student-friendly' teachers.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique in deep learning, initially designed for model compression. This process involves training a compact "student" model to replicate the behavior of a larger, more powerful "teacher" model, enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art networks in resource-constrained environments. Beyond creating smaller and faster models, the paradigm has evolved significantly. It now serves as a versatile framework for a wide range of tasks, including improving model interpretability, enabling training without access to original data, enhancing generalization, and facilitating collaborative learning in federated settings. This demonstrates that knowledge distillation is not just a compression tool but a foundational method for making advanced artificial intelligence more practical, adaptable, and widely applicable.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Enhancement in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning where a compact "student" model is trained to mimic a larger, more complex "teacher" model. The primary goal is to create smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. This is achieved by transferring the rich knowledge embedded in the teacher's outputs or internal feature representations to the student. The applications of this versatile framework are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. Beyond simply reducing model size, knowledge distillation is also used to enhance student model performance, improve generalization, and address challenges such as data privacy and algorithmic fairness.

papers_seen.author: Harvey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression and Optimization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning for model compression and knowledge transfer. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model or an ensemble of teachers. The primary goal is to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. This method is not only used for reducing model size and inference latency but also for enhancing the performance of student models across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. By transferring knowledge through mechanisms like soft labels or intermediate feature representations, knowledge distillation has become a versatile tool for developing efficient and accurate neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. This process enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. By training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs, including the nuanced probability distributions over classes, the student model can achieve performance far superior to what it could by training on the ground-truth labels alone. This method has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts while being significantly faster and smaller.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly large language and vision models, have achieved state-of-the-art performance but are often computationally expensive and memory-intensive, hindering their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Model compression techniques address this challenge by creating smaller, more efficient models without significant performance degradation. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible method for this purpose. This process involves training a compact "student" network to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" network. By transferring the rich "dark knowledge" from the teacher, such as class relationship information or intermediate feature representations, the student model can achieve performance comparable to its larger counterpart. This approach has proven effective across a wide range of applications, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, demonstrating its versatility in making advanced AI more accessible and practical.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Effective Strategy for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques have emerged as a critical field of study to address these issues. Knowledge distillation, a prominent compression method, involves training a smaller 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student model to achieve performance far exceeding what it could attain by training on ground-truth labels alone. This approach has proven versatile, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, leading to models that are not only smaller and faster but also maintain high levels of accuracy, facilitating the practical application of state-of-the-art deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Deep neural networks have become increasingly large and complex, which hinders their deployment on devices with limited computational resources. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. This method involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" network to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" network or an ensemble of models. The student learns to reproduce the teacher's outputs or its internal representations, effectively transferring the rich knowledge learned by the larger model. This process enables the creation of compact models that maintain high performance across a variety of domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning, without requiring architectural changes or additional data.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression paradigm where a compact 'student' model learns from a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This technique aims to create smaller, more efficient networks that retain the high performance of their cumbersome counterparts, making them suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Initially focused on mimicking output probabilities, the field has evolved to encompass a wide range of applications beyond simple classification, including complex tasks in natural language processing and computer vision. The effectiveness of distillation is now understood to hinge on more sophisticated methods, such as transferring knowledge from internal feature representations and adapting the process to transfer specific qualities like adversarial robustness. Modern approaches integrate distillation with other compression techniques and advanced training strategies, demonstrating its versatility and importance in developing state-of-the-art, deployable deep learning models.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique that facilitates the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. This is achieved by training the student to mimic the outputs or internal representations of the teacher. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. Advanced methods have been developed to address specific challenges, such as transferring adversarial robustness, performing distillation without access to original training data, mitigating biases, and improving the interaction between teacher and student models.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in which a smaller, more efficient "student" model is trained to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. The primary objective is to transfer the rich knowledge from the cumbersome teacher to the compact student, enabling the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. This process creates smaller and faster models that maintain high accuracy. The versatility of knowledge distillation is demonstrated by its successful application across diverse domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning. Advanced methods have been developed that extend beyond the basic teacher-student paradigm to further enhance knowledge transfer and address complex learning scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, the 'student'. This process enables the deployment of high-performing deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. The fundamental approach involves training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs, but numerous variations have been developed to enhance this process. These include distilling knowledge from intermediate feature representations, using multiple teachers for domain adaptation or multi-task learning, and applying distillation in specialized areas like object detection and graph neural networks. Advanced methods address challenges such as the absence of training data, the propagation of model biases, and applications in privacy-preserving federated learning. By leveraging knowledge from more capable models, distillation significantly improves the performance of compact networks across a wide range of tasks in natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions suitable for real-world deployment. This process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. While the primary goal is to reduce computational and memory requirements for resource-constrained environments, the applications of knowledge distillation extend far beyond simple model compression. The technique has proven to be a versatile framework for enhancing student model performance, improving generalization, adapting models to new domains, and enabling knowledge transfer in complex scenarios such as lifelong learning. This makes it a fundamental tool for creating more practical, robust, and efficient artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly in fields like natural language processing, have grown significantly in size and computational cost, posing challenges for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Model compression aims to create smaller, more efficient models while retaining high performance. Knowledge distillation is a prominent compression paradigm where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger 'teacher' model. This approach transfers the learned knowledge of the teacher, enabling the smaller student to achieve better performance than if trained alone. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains, with research exploring advanced techniques such as transferring knowledge from intermediate layers, using multiple teachers, and performing distillation without access to the original training data.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning for model compression and performance improvement. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. Traditionally, this is achieved by using the teacher's softened output probabilities as supervisory signals for the student. However, recent advancements have explored mimicking intermediate feature representations, which can provide richer information. The applications of knowledge distillation are diverse, extending to compressing large language models, improving low-precision networks, and enabling collaborative training in privacy-sensitive settings like federated learning. Furthermore, research challenges the conventional view of a superior teacher guiding a weaker student, suggesting that the regularization effect of the process is a key component of its success, even leading to teacher-free distillation frameworks.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and computational expense of state-of-the-art deep learning models present significant barriers to their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile model compression technique to address this challenge. This method involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to mimic the outputs and internal representations of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student model can achieve comparable or even superior performance while being significantly smaller and faster. This approach has proven effective across a wide range of applications in natural language processing and computer vision, enabling the practical deployment of advanced AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing complexity of deep learning models has created significant challenges for their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible model compression technique to address this issue. This method involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model, effectively transferring its learned knowledge. This process enables the creation of smaller, faster models that retain high performance, making them suitable for practical applications. The versatility of knowledge distillation is demonstrated by its successful application across diverse domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning, as well as in specialized contexts like data-free learning and enhancing model interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent model compression technique to address the challenges posed by the increasing size and complexity of deep learning models. This method involves a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, more cumbersome 'teacher' model. The goal is to transfer the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the creation of compact, fast models that retain high performance. This makes state-of-the-art deep learning more accessible for deployment in resource-constrained or latency-sensitive environments, such as mobile devices. The technique has proven successful and versatile across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to address the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in resource-constrained environments. The process involves a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This knowledge transfer allows the student to achieve high performance while maintaining a significantly smaller footprint, making it suitable for practical applications. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile paradigm used for improving model generalization, enabling training without access to original data, and facilitating learning in complex settings like federated learning.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for Vision-to-Sensor Action Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) based on multi-modal approach has been recently shown to improve the accuracy performance of HAR. However, restricted computational resources associated with wearable devices, i.e., smartwatch, failed to directly support such advanced methods. To tackle this issue, this study introduces an end-to-end Vision-to-Sensor Knowledge Distillation (VSKD) framework. In this VSKD framework, only time-series data, i.e., accelerometer data, is needed from wearable devices during the testing phase. Therefore, this framework will not only reduce the computational demands on edge devices, but also produce a learning model that closely matches the performance of the computational expensive multi-modal approach. In order to retain the local temporal relationship and facilitate visual deep learning models, we first convert time-series data to two-dimensional images by applying the Gramian Angular Field ( GAF) based encoding method. We adopted ResNet18 and multi-scale TRN with BN-Inception as teacher and student network in this study, respectively. A novel loss function, named Distance and Angle-wised Semantic Knowledge loss (DASK), is proposed to mitigate the modality variations between the vision and the sensor domain. Extensive experimental results on UTD-MHAD, MMAct, and Berkeley-MHAD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed VSKD model which can deployed on wearable sensors.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to transfer the rich knowledge from the teacher, thereby creating a compact model that retains high performance while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. This enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated through its application across diverse tasks and the continuous development of advanced methods that go beyond simple output matching, solidifying its role in making advanced artificial intelligence more practical and accessible.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Carney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Paradigm for Model Compression and Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning for model compression and knowledge transfer. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process allows for the creation of smaller, more efficient models that retain a significant portion of the original model's performance, making them suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Advances in this field have expanded its application beyond simple compression, with methods developed for distilling knowledge from intermediate features, ensembles of teachers, and even in scenarios where the original training data is unavailable. The versatility of knowledge distillation has led to its successful application in numerous areas, including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique where a compact 'student' model learns from a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process aims to transfer the teacher's learned knowledge, enabling the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost. The transfer can occur through various means, including mimicking the teacher's output probabilities or its internal feature representations. Advanced methods have emerged, such as online distillation where models teach each other, and meta-learning approaches where the teacher adapts its training strategy to better instruct the student. This technique has found broad applications in both natural language processing and computer vision, enabling the deployment of sophisticated models in resource-constrained environments by creating efficient, task-specific networks for tasks ranging from language understanding to 3D object detection.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient ones. This process involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a pre-trained, cumbersome 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to retain the high performance of the teacher model while significantly reducing computational and storage costs, making advanced models deployable on resource-constrained devices. The applications of knowledge distillation are broad, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and healthcare. Beyond simple output matching, advanced methods focus on transferring knowledge from intermediate feature representations and using adversarial techniques to improve the student's learning process. This versatility makes knowledge distillation a crucial tool for optimizing and deploying state-of-the-art neural networks in real-world scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that addresses the challenge of deploying large, complex models in resource-constrained environments. The process involves a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This knowledge transfer allows the student to achieve high accuracy without the computational overhead of the teacher. The versatility of this framework has led to its successful application across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making it a critical tool for developing practical and accessible artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models, particularly in fields like natural language processing, present significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible model compression technique to address these challenges. This approach involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, including its predictions on unlabeled data, the student model can achieve comparable performance to its larger counterpart while being significantly smaller and faster. This technique has proven effective across a wide range of applications, from compressing large language models to enabling efficient object detection and transferring knowledge across different data modalities, making it a critical tool for creating practical, real-world artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary objective is to reduce the computational and memory requirements of state-of-the-art models, enabling their deployment in resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. This is achieved by training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs, which provide richer supervisory signals than traditional training labels. The technique has evolved beyond simple compression, proving to be a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, transferring knowledge across different tasks, and enabling novel applications in areas like privacy-preserving machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Harmon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary objective is to reduce computational and memory requirements, enabling the deployment of powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining high performance. This is typically achieved by training the student to mimic the teacher's behavior, often using its output probabilities as supervisory signals. The technique has found wide application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile framework used to enhance model performance, facilitate privacy-preserving distributed learning, and adapt models to new domains.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, such as mobile phones, without a significant loss in accuracy. The student model learns from the rich information contained in the teacher's outputs, including class probabilities and intermediate feature representations. This technique has found broad applications across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, not only for creating smaller and faster models but also for improving model robustness, generalization, and interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: The Expanding Role of Knowledge Distillation in Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning where knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model is transferred to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. Originally conceived as a method for model compression, its applications have expanded significantly. This technique not only enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments but also serves as a mechanism to enhance the performance of student models beyond what they could achieve through standard training. The versatility of knowledge distillation is demonstrated by its application across diverse domains, from natural language processing to computer vision. Recent advancements have introduced more dynamic and effective distillation frameworks, such as online and self-distillation, and have even leveraged the technique to improve model interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Effective Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly large-scale language models, have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous tasks. However, their significant computational and memory requirements hinder deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student model can achieve comparable performance with a fraction of the parameters and faster inference speeds. This approach has proven effective across various domains, including Natural Language Processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning, enabling the practical application of complex neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm designed to reduce the size and computational cost of large deep learning models. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to transfer the generalized knowledge from the cumbersome teacher to the lightweight student, creating a compact model suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. This is often achieved by training the student on the richer, soft probability distributions from the teacher's outputs. The technique has been successfully applied across a wide range of domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and has evolved to include more advanced methods beyond simple output matching.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Lambert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The primary objective is to enable the deployment of powerful, state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices by reducing their size and computational requirements without a substantial loss in performance. The process typically involves training the student to mimic the rich output distributions of the teacher, which contain more information than simple ground-truth labels. The applications of this paradigm are extensive, spanning natural language processing and computer vision. Advanced methods have evolved to include transferring knowledge from intermediate layers, using multiple teachers, and extending the technique's utility beyond compression to areas such as improving model robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.
