papers_seen.author: Velasquez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a deep learning technique primarily used for model compression, where a smaller 'student' model learns from a larger 'teacher' model. This process facilitates the deployment of powerful but cumbersome models on resource-constrained devices by reducing their computational and memory footprint. The student model is trained to mimic the teacher's outputs, effectively transferring its learned knowledge and generalization capabilities. While initially developed for creating efficient models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now used to enhance model performance, improve fairness, and enable learning in specialized contexts like federated learning and domain adaptation. The evolution of methods, such as distilling information from intermediate layers or using self-distillation, highlights its transformation into a versatile and fundamental framework for optimizing deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous tasks, but their large size and computational expense often hinder their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. This method involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model, effectively transferring the teacher's learned knowledge. This process allows for the creation of compact models that are significantly faster and smaller, yet retain a high level of performance. Knowledge distillation has proven to be a flexible and effective strategy across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, enabling the development of powerful and practical AI applications.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique in deep learning for model compression and performance enhancement. Operating on a teacher-student framework, it enables the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex model to a smaller, more efficient one. The primary objective is to create compact yet powerful models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without significant performance degradation. This versatile approach has found wide-ranging applications in natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition. Its utility extends beyond mere compression, serving to improve model generalization, enable privacy-preserving distributed learning, and even allow student models to surpass their teachers in performance.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique where a compact 'student' model learns from a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process aims to transfer the teacher's learned knowledge, enabling the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost. The transfer can occur through various means, including mimicking the teacher's output probabilities or its internal feature representations. Advanced methods have emerged, such as online distillation where models teach each other, and meta-learning approaches where the teacher adapts its training strategy to better instruct the student. This technique has found broad applications in both natural language processing and computer vision, enabling the deployment of sophisticated models in resource-constrained environments by creating efficient, task-specific networks for tasks ranging from language understanding to 3D object detection.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models without substantial performance degradation. The process involves transferring knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a compact 'student' model. This allows for the deployment of powerful neural networks in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. The student learns to mimic the rich output distributions and internal representations of the teacher, thereby inheriting its capabilities while maintaining a smaller footprint. This versatile framework has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and its applications extend beyond compression to areas like performance enhancement, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, faster, and more efficient models without substantial performance degradation. This paradigm involves training a compact "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, more complex "teacher" model. By transferring the rich knowledge embedded in the teacher, this process enables the deployment of state-of-the-art architectures in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices and edge hardware. Its applications are widespread, spanning numerous fields including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, demonstrating its effectiveness in making advanced AI more practical and accessible.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Distilling Object Detectors with Fine-grained Feature Imitation
papers_seen.abstract: State-of-the-art CNN based recognition models are often computationally prohibitive to deploy on low-end devices. A promising high level approach tackling this limitation is knowledge distillation, which let small student model mimic cumbersome teacher model's output to get improved generalization. However, related methods mainly focus on simple task of classification while do not consider complex tasks like object detection. We show applying the vanilla knowledge distillation to detection model gets minor gain. To address the challenge of distilling knowledge in detection model, we propose a fine-grained feature imitation method exploiting the cross-location discrepancy of feature response. Our intuition is that detectors care more about local near object regions. Thus the discrepancy of feature response on the near object anchor locations reveals important information of how teacher model tends to generalize. We design a novel mechanism to estimate those locations and let student model imitate the teacher on them to get enhanced performance. We first validate the idea on a developed lightweight toy detector which carries simplest notion of current state-of-the-art anchor based detection models on challenging KITTI dataset, our method generates up to 15% boost of mAP for the student model compared to the non-imitated counterpart. We then extensively evaluate the method with Faster R-CNN model under various scenarios with common object detection benchmark of Pascal VOC and COCO, imitation alleviates up to 74% performance drop of student model compared to teacher. Codes released at https://github.com/twangnh/Distilling-Object-Detectors

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, the 'student'. This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by significantly reducing their size and computational footprint while retaining high performance. The core idea involves training the student model to replicate the teacher's output probabilities, which contain richer information than simple class labels. Advanced methods also involve distilling knowledge from the teacher's intermediate feature representations, using multiple teachers, or even operating without access to the original training data. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across a wide range of applications, including natural language processing, speech recognition, computer vision, and for improving model interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful paradigm in deep learning for compressing large, computationally expensive models into smaller, more efficient versions without a significant loss in performance. This process involves a "student" model learning to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By training on the soft probability distributions or intermediate feature representations produced by the teacher, the student model can learn richer information and achieve better generalization than if it were trained solely on hard labels. This technique extends beyond simple model compression, enabling the transfer of inductive biases, performance improvements through self-distillation, and the unification of knowledge from multiple models. Its applications are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and privacy-preserving federated learning, making it a crucial tool for deploying state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm designed to reduce the size and computational cost of large deep learning models. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to transfer the generalized knowledge from the cumbersome teacher to the lightweight student, creating a compact model suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. This is often achieved by training the student on the richer, soft probability distributions from the teacher's outputs. The technique has been successfully applied across a wide range of domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and has evolved to include more advanced methods beyond simple output matching.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Model Compression and Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large, complex deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. This process typically involves a teacher-student framework, where a smaller student model learns to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This paradigm addresses the significant computational and storage costs associated with state-of-the-art models in fields like Natural Language Processing and computer vision. Various methods have been developed to tackle challenges such as data privacy, architectural mismatches between teacher and student, and information transfer efficiency. Applications are diverse, ranging from compressing large language models and generative adversarial networks to enhancing model robustness against adversarial attacks and enabling efficient federated learning. Extensions to the basic framework include using multiple teachers, adversarial learning, and data-free distillation techniques, continually expanding the utility of this compression strategy.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient models without significant performance degradation. The process involves a teacher-student framework, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This knowledge transfer allows for the deployment of complex neural networks on resource-constrained devices, such as mobile phones. While primarily used for compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving fairness and interpretability, and enabling complex learning paradigms like federated learning. The technique has been successfully applied across numerous domains, most notably in Natural Language Processing (NLP) for compressing large language models and in computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for model compression and performance enhancement in deep learning. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student network is trained to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process facilitates the creation of compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. Methodologies have evolved beyond simply mimicking output predictions to include transferring knowledge from intermediate feature representations, employing multiple teachers, and selectively applying the teacher's knowledge. These advanced strategies have found broad applications across natural language processing and computer vision, enabling the compression of large language models, improving machine translation, and even enhancing algorithmic fairness.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression and knowledge transfer technique in deep learning. The technique is versatile, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, and has given rise to numerous variations, including self-distillation, data-free distillation, and methods involving multiple or adaptive teachers.

Advanced methods have expanded upon the traditional framework, introducing data-free distillation, meta-learning approaches where the teacher adapts its teaching strategy, and multi-teacher setups. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has also been leveraged to enhance model interpretability and improve generalization across different data distributions, demonstrating its versatility as a powerful tool in the development of practical deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful training paradigm where a smaller "student" model learns from a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. Initially conceived for model compression, this technique enables the development of lightweight, efficient neural networks that retain the high performance of their cumbersome counterparts. Beyond creating faster and smaller models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now a crucial tool for a range of tasks including domain adaptation, where models must adjust to new data distributions, and federated learning, which facilitates collaborative training across distributed devices with heterogeneous models without sharing private data. The success of distillation often depends on sophisticated strategies that go beyond simple output matching, such as aligning intermediate feature representations and leveraging statistically sound data augmentation. Despite its power, challenges in optimization remain, but knowledge distillation continues to be a versatile and impactful framework in modern deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous domains, but their large size and computational expense often hinder deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and effective model compression technique to address this challenge. The process involves a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge embedded in the teacher's predictions or internal representations, the student can achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer parameters. The utility of this framework has expanded beyond simple compression, proving effective for enhancing model performance, transferring specific capabilities like adversarial robustness, and even mitigating societal biases within language models. Advanced methods such as self-distillation, online distillation, and data-free approaches further increase its versatility, making it a critical tool for developing efficient and practical AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Towards Understanding Ensemble, Knowledge Distillation and Self-Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We formally study how ensemble of deep learning models can improve test accuracy, and how the superior performance of ensemble can be distilled into a single model using knowledge distillation. We consider the challenging case where the ensemble is simply an average of the outputs of a few independently trained neural networks with the SAME architecture, trained using the SAME algorithm on the SAME data set, and they only differ by the random seeds used in the initialization.   We show that ensemble/knowledge distillation in Deep Learning works very differently from traditional learning theory (such as boosting or NTKs, neural tangent kernels). To properly understand them, we develop a theory showing that when data has a structure we refer to as ``multi-view'', then ensemble of independently trained neural networks can provably improve test accuracy, and such superior test accuracy can also be provably distilled into a single model by training a single model to match the output of the ensemble instead of the true label. Our result sheds light on how ensemble works in deep learning in a way that is completely different from traditional theorems, and how the ``dark knowledge'' is hidden in the outputs of the ensemble and can be used in distillation. In the end, we prove that self-distillation can also be viewed as implicitly combining ensemble and knowledge distillation to improve test accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly large-scale language models in Natural Language Processing (NLP), have achieved state-of-the-art performance but are often too large and slow for practical deployment. Model compression techniques are essential for creating smaller, more efficient models. Knowledge distillation is a popular compression paradigm where a compact "student" model learns from a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This process involves transferring the teacher's knowledge, often through its output probabilities or internal representations, to guide the student's training. Advanced methods have emerged, including multi-teacher distillation, self-distillation, and data-free approaches that work without the original training data. Knowledge distillation can also be combined with other compression methods like pruning and quantization to further enhance model efficiency, making powerful deep learning models accessible for resource-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance in many fields, but their large size and computational demands often prevent their use in resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques address this issue, with knowledge distillation emerging as a prominent and versatile paradigm. This method involves a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The process transfers the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher to the student, enabling the creation of compact models that are faster and require less memory. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation can also enhance the performance and generalization of the student model, making it a powerful tool for optimizing neural networks for practical deployment.

papers_seen.author: West
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework Beyond Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a pivotal technique in deep learning, initially conceived as a method for model compression. This process involves transferring knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model, enabling the deployment of powerful neural networks in resource-constrained environments. However, the utility of knowledge distillation extends far beyond simple compression. It serves as a powerful framework for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and increasing the interpretability of opaque "black-box" models. By leveraging the rich, nuanced information captured by teacher models, knowledge distillation can guide student models to achieve superior accuracy, sometimes even surpassing their teachers, and can transform complex neural networks into simpler, more transparent structures like decision trees. This makes it a versatile and indispensable tool in the modern deep learning and natural language processing toolkit.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Shields
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The primary objective is to create compact models that can be deployed on resource-constrained devices, such as mobile phones, without a substantial loss in performance. This is achieved by training the student model to mimic the outputs or internal feature representations of the teacher. This versatile framework has been widely applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, not only for creating smaller and faster models but also for enhancing model robustness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a significant loss in performance. The core idea involves training the student not only on the ground-truth data but also using the outputs or intermediate representations of the trained teacher as a richer, soft target. This method has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and recommender systems, leading to a wide range of lightweight models that retain the capabilities of their larger counterparts.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Davenport
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient neural networks. This is achieved through a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to replicate the behavior and knowledge of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. While the primary goal is to enable the deployment of complex models on resource-constrained devices, the applications of knowledge distillation extend further. The technique has been shown to enhance the performance and generalization of student models, and it serves as a flexible framework for transferring desirable properties such as algorithmic fairness, robustness, and knowledge in continual learning scenarios. Its utility across diverse domains like natural language processing and computer vision makes it a multifaceted tool in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning where a compact "student" model is trained to replicate the performance of a larger, more complex "teacher" model. This process serves not only as a method for model compression, making large neural networks deployable on resource-constrained devices, but also as a versatile training strategy to enhance model performance. By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, students can achieve improved generalization, faster convergence, and even superior accuracy. This approach has demonstrated success across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition, proving its flexibility and effectiveness in creating more efficient and robust machine learning models.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for model compression and performance optimization in deep learning. It involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student to achieve comparable or even superior performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost. Various strategies have been developed, including distilling knowledge from the teacher's final outputs, internal feature representations, or an ensemble of multiple teachers. This methodology has been successfully applied across a wide range of domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and federated learning, to create compact, fast, and effective models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, the 'student'. This process enables the deployment of high-performing deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. The fundamental approach involves training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs, but numerous variations have been developed to enhance this process. These include distilling knowledge from intermediate feature representations, using multiple teachers for domain adaptation or multi-task learning, and applying distillation in specialized areas like object detection and graph neural networks. Advanced methods address challenges such as the absence of training data, the propagation of model biases, and applications in privacy-preserving federated learning. By leveraging knowledge from more capable models, distillation significantly improves the performance of compact networks across a wide range of tasks in natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Wide Neural Networks: Risk Bound, Data Efficiency and Imperfect Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a strategy of training a student network with guide of the soft output from a teacher network. It has been a successful method of model compression and knowledge transfer. However, currently knowledge distillation lacks a convincing theoretical understanding. On the other hand, recent finding on neural tangent kernel enables us to approximate a wide neural network with a linear model of the network's random features. In this paper, we theoretically analyze the knowledge distillation of a wide neural network. First we provide a transfer risk bound for the linearized model of the network. Then we propose a metric of the task's training difficulty, called data inefficiency. Based on this metric, we show that for a perfect teacher, a high ratio of teacher's soft labels can be beneficial. Finally, for the case of imperfect teacher, we find that hard labels can correct teacher's wrong prediction, which explains the practice of mixing hard and soft labels.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly in fields like natural language processing, have grown significantly in size and computational cost, posing challenges for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Model compression aims to create smaller, more efficient models while retaining high performance. Knowledge distillation is a prominent compression paradigm where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger 'teacher' model. This approach transfers the learned knowledge of the teacher, enabling the smaller student to achieve better performance than if trained alone. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains, with research exploring advanced techniques such as transferring knowledge from intermediate layers, using multiple teachers, and performing distillation without access to the original training data.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. The recent poster child of this trend is the deep language representation model, which includes BERT, ELMo, and GPT. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has produced increasingly large and complex models that achieve state-of-the-art performance but are often impractical for deployment due to their computational and memory requirements. Model compression techniques, particularly knowledge distillation, address this challenge by transferring knowledge from a large, cumbersome 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process enables the creation of compact models that retain a significant portion of the teacher's performance, making them suitable for resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. The flexibility of knowledge distillation is evident in its successful application across various domains, including natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph-based learning, as well as its adaptability to scenarios where the original training data is unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, faster, and more efficient models without substantial performance degradation. This paradigm involves training a compact "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, more complex "teacher" model. By transferring the rich knowledge embedded in the teacher, this process enables the deployment of state-of-the-art architectures in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices and edge hardware. Its applications are widespread, spanning numerous fields including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, demonstrating its effectiveness in making advanced AI more practical and accessible.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: From Model Compression to a Versatile Deep Learning Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a key technique in deep learning, initially developed for model compression. It involves a teacher-student paradigm where a compact "student" model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, more powerful "teacher" model. This process allows for the creation of smaller, faster models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. While its primary application is compression, the utility of knowledge distillation has expanded considerably. It is now used to enhance model performance, facilitate learning in data-scarce environments, and enable advanced paradigms like federated and lifelong learning, establishing it as a versatile framework for building more efficient and robust AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Paradigm for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Originally conceived as a method for a smaller "student" model to learn from a larger "teacher" model, the paradigm has evolved significantly. Research now shows that the benefits of distillation extend beyond simple mimicry, with the regularization effects of soft labels playing a crucial role. This technique has proven effective in a wide array of complex domains, including natural language processing for text generation and translation, the compression of generative adversarial networks, and the optimization of graph neural networks. Advanced methods such as self-distillation, adversarial training, and extensions for domain adaptation further highlight its versatility. Ultimately, knowledge distillation is a critical tool for creating efficient, yet powerful, AI systems suitable for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient models from larger, complex ones. This process typically involves a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model learns to mimic the behavior and outputs of a pre-trained teacher model. The primary goal is to enable the deployment of state-of-the-art architectures, such as large language models, on resource-constrained devices where computational power and memory are limited. The applications of this technique are diverse, spanning natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simple size reduction, knowledge distillation is also used to enhance model performance, improve generalization, and transfer knowledge in privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile and Effective Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models have achieved remarkable performance but their large size and computational expense often hinder their deployment in practical, resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile model compression framework to address this challenge. This technique involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, the student can achieve comparable or even superior performance while being significantly smaller and faster. The applications of this framework are extensive, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. Moreover, advanced methods have extended its utility to scenarios where training data is unavailable and have demonstrated benefits beyond simple compression, such as improving model robustness. Knowledge distillation effectively bridges the gap between high-performance research models and practical, deployable AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of compact, efficient models suitable for real-world deployment. Operating on a teacher-student paradigm, it involves transferring knowledge from a large, complex model to a smaller one. This process reduces the computational and memory footprint of the student model, allowing powerful architectures to run on resource-constrained devices. While initially conceived for compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now used across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, not only to create smaller models but also to enhance performance, improve generalization, and enable novel capabilities like cross-modal learning.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly large-scale language models in Natural Language Processing (NLP), have achieved state-of-the-art performance but are often too large and slow for practical deployment. Model compression techniques are essential for creating smaller, more efficient models. Knowledge distillation is a popular compression paradigm where a compact "student" model learns from a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This process involves transferring the teacher's knowledge, often through its output probabilities or internal representations, to guide the student's training. Advanced methods have emerged, including multi-teacher distillation, self-distillation, and data-free approaches that work without the original training data. Knowledge distillation can also be combined with other compression methods like pruning and quantization to further enhance model efficiency, making powerful deep learning models accessible for resource-constrained applications.
