papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression paradigm designed to create efficient, lightweight "student" deep learning models by transferring knowledge from larger, more powerful "teacher" models. This process enables the deployment of state-of-the-art networks in resource-constrained environments. The methods for knowledge transfer have evolved from matching output probabilities to more sophisticated techniques that focus on mimicking intermediate feature representations. Innovations in the field include adversarial training frameworks, the application of automated machine learning for architecture search, and even teacher-free approaches that leverage self-distillation as a form of regularization. Knowledge distillation has demonstrated significant success across a wide range of applications, including the compression of large language models in natural language processing, the simplification of complex graph neural networks, and the optimization of models in federated learning and speech recognition systems.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Harvey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression and Optimization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning for model compression and knowledge transfer. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model or an ensemble of teachers. The primary goal is to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. This method is not only used for reducing model size and inference latency but also for enhancing the performance of student models across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. By transferring knowledge through mechanisms like soft labels or intermediate feature representations, knowledge distillation has become a versatile tool for developing efficient and accurate neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, the 'student'. This process enables the deployment of high-performing deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. The fundamental approach involves training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs, but numerous variations have been developed to enhance this process. These include distilling knowledge from intermediate feature representations, using multiple teachers for domain adaptation or multi-task learning, and applying distillation in specialized areas like object detection and graph neural networks. Advanced methods address challenges such as the absence of training data, the propagation of model biases, and applications in privacy-preserving federated learning. By leveraging knowledge from more capable models, distillation significantly improves the performance of compact networks across a wide range of tasks in natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large, state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This process involves training a smaller 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The core principle is to transfer the nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, often encapsulated in its soft predictions, to the more compact student network. This approach has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, to compress models like large language transformers and generative adversarial networks. Advanced methods have been developed that utilize multiple teachers, distill knowledge from intermediate layers, and even operate in data-free settings to address privacy concerns. Furthermore, knowledge distillation plays a crucial role in communication-efficient frameworks like federated learning, demonstrating its versatility and importance in modern machine learning.

The transfer of knowledge can occur by replicating the teacher's output predictions, its internal representations, or by using more advanced methods like adversarial learning. This technique has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing for compressing large language models, computer vision for efficient image recognition and synthesis, and even in specialized fields like medical imaging and federated learning.

papers_seen.author: Hall

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning. The primary goal is to reduce computational and storage costs, making large models deployable on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. This technique has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing for compressing large language models, computer vision for optimizing generative networks, and reinforcement learning for policy transfer. Advanced methods have expanded upon the traditional framework, introducing data-free distillation, meta-learning approaches where the teacher adapts its teaching strategy, and multi-teacher setups. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has also been leveraged to enhance model interpretability and improve generalization across different data distributions, demonstrating its versatility as a powerful tool in the development of practical deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Wilson

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a prominent technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. The process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This approach addresses the significant computational and memory challenges associated with deploying state-of-the-art neural networks in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, student models can achieve comparable performance with a significantly smaller footprint. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated by its successful application across diverse domains and its adaptation to address challenges like data privacy and architectural mismatches, making advanced AI more accessible for real-world use.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Keith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Paradigm for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. It facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient 'student' models by transferring knowledge from larger, more complex 'teacher' models. This process enables the deployment of powerful neural networks on devices with limited computational and storage resources. The applications of this technique are widespread, moving beyond simple size reduction to include performance enhancement, improvements in model interpretability, and addressing algorithmic fairness. By leveraging the rich information captured by teacher models, distillation provides a flexible and powerful framework for optimizing deep learning systems for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Robust and Resource-Efficient Data-Free Knowledge Distillation by Generative Pseudo Replay
papers_seen.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows knowledge transfer from a trained neural network (teacher) to a more compact one (student) in the absence of original training data. Existing works use a validation set to monitor the accuracy of the student over real data and report the highest performance throughout the entire process. However, validation data may not be available at distillation time either, making it infeasible to record the student snapshot that achieved the peak accuracy. Therefore, a practical data-free KD method should be robust and ideally provide monotonically increasing student accuracy during distillation. This is challenging because the student experiences knowledge degradation due to the distribution shift of the synthetic data. A straightforward approach to overcome this issue is to store and rehearse the generated samples periodically, which increases the memory footprint and creates privacy concerns. We propose to model the distribution of the previously observed synthetic samples with a generative network. In particular, we design a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a training objective that is customized to learn the synthetic data representations optimally. The student is rehearsed by the generative pseudo replay technique, with samples produced by the VAE. Hence knowledge degradation can be prevented without storing any samples. Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that our method optimizes the expected value of the distilled model accuracy while eliminating the large memory overhead incurred by the sample-storing methods.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a pivotal technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions. This process involves a teacher-student framework where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger teacher model. The primary benefit is enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, where computational power and memory are limited. The applications of this technique are widespread, spanning natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simple model size reduction, knowledge distillation is also used to enhance a model's performance, transfer beneficial properties between architectures, and improve generalization.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient models without a significant loss in performance. The process involves a teacher-student framework, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This transfer of knowledge allows for the deployment of state-of-the-art architectures, such as large language models, in resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. The methodology extends beyond simple output imitation to include transferring knowledge from intermediate feature layers and has led to advanced strategies like data-free distillation and meta-learning approaches. Ultimately, knowledge distillation serves as a versatile tool for developing practical, efficient, and robust artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, cumbersome teacher model to a smaller, more efficient student model. This process enables the deployment of complex deep learning architectures on resource-constrained devices by reducing model size and inference latency without a significant loss in performance. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing tasks like question answering and machine translation, as well as computer vision domains such as object detection and action recognition. Various methods have been developed, including multi-teacher frameworks, data-free distillation, and fine-grained feature imitation, to improve the knowledge transfer process. These techniques not only facilitate model compression but can also enhance the student model's generalization capabilities and, in some cases, lead to performance that is comparable or even superior to the original teacher model.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a prominent technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. The process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This approach addresses the significant computational and memory challenges associated with deploying state-of-the-art neural networks in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, student models can achieve comparable performance with a significantly smaller footprint. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated by its successful application across diverse domains and its adaptation to address challenges like data privacy and architectural mismatches, making advanced AI more accessible for real-world use.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions suitable for real-world deployment. This process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. While the primary goal is to reduce computational and memory requirements for resource-constrained environments, the applications of knowledge distillation extend far beyond simple model compression. The technique has proven to be a versatile framework for enhancing student model performance, improving generalization, adapting models to new domains, and enabling knowledge transfer in complex scenarios such as lifelong learning. This makes it a fundamental tool for creating more practical, robust, and efficient artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly in fields like natural language processing, have grown significantly in size and computational cost, posing challenges for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Model compression aims to create smaller, more efficient models while retaining high performance. Knowledge distillation is a prominent compression paradigm where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger 'teacher' model. This approach transfers the learned knowledge of the teacher, enabling the smaller student to achieve better performance than if trained alone. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains, with research exploring advanced techniques such as transferring knowledge from intermediate layers, using multiple teachers, and performing distillation without access to the original training data.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective model compression technique that facilitates the deployment of large, complex deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, including its understanding of data structure and inter-class relationships, the student model can achieve performance far superior to what it could by training on the data alone. This approach has proven successful across various domains, including natural language processing, speech recognition, and computer vision, enabling the creation of compact models that are faster and require less memory without a significant drop in accuracy. The flexibility of knowledge distillation allows it to be combined with other techniques like data augmentation and federated learning, extending its applicability to diverse and challenging scenarios such as privacy-preservation and few-shot learning.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient neural networks. This is achieved through a teacher-student framework, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the outputs and internal representations of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of complex models, enabling their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation also serves as a versatile tool for enhancing the performance and interpretability of student models. The technique has been successfully applied across a wide array of domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, with ongoing research refining the methods for knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Effective Strategy for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques have emerged as a critical field of study to address these issues. Knowledge distillation, a prominent compression method, involves training a smaller 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student model to achieve performance far exceeding what it could attain by training on ground-truth labels alone. This approach has proven versatile, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, leading to models that are not only smaller and faster but also maintain high levels of accuracy, facilitating the practical application of state-of-the-art deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prevalent model compression technique used to create smaller, more efficient "student" neural networks that learn from larger, more complex "teacher" models. This process transfers the knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student to achieve high performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost. The applications of this technique are broad, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and graph-based machine learning. Methods range from mimicking the teacher's output predictions to more advanced techniques like imitating intermediate feature representations. Researchers have also developed specialized distillation strategies for complex tasks, data-scarce scenarios, and for transferring properties like adversarial robustness, making it a versatile tool for deploying state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique in deep learning, primarily known for model compression. This process involves a teacher-student framework where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, cumbersome teacher model. The primary objective is to enable the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments by reducing computational and memory demands without a substantial loss in performance. However, the utility of knowledge distillation extends far beyond simple model compression. It has evolved into a versatile paradigm for addressing complex challenges such as domain adaptation, continual learning, and privacy preservation. By transferring knowledge in various forms, from output probabilities to intermediate feature representations, this framework enhances model efficiency, robustness, and adaptability across a wide range of applications in natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning designed to compress large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions. The process involves training a compact "student" model to mimic the behavior and outputs of a pre-trained, high-performance "teacher" model. This knowledge transfer enables the deployment of powerful artificial intelligence systems in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a substantial loss in accuracy. While originally conceived for model compression, the applications of distillation have expanded significantly, now serving as a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling advanced learning paradigms like domain adaptation and federated learning.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Paradigm for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a versatile and powerful technique for model compression within deep learning. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process facilitates the deployment of complex, state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices by reducing their size and computational requirements. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation also serves as a method to enhance student model performance, improve generalization, and enable novel applications in areas like privacy-preserving learning and cross-modal knowledge transfer. Its flexibility has led to widespread adoption and research across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Chandler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient models from larger, more complex ones. This technique operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary goal is to enable the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile or edge devices. This process allows the student to inherit the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, resulting in a lightweight model that retains high performance. The applications of knowledge distillation are diverse, extending beyond simple compression to areas like domain adaptation, federated learning, and improving model interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of compact, efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger, more complex teacher models. This teacher-student learning paradigm enables the deployment of powerful neural networks in resource-constrained environments, such as on mobile devices, without a significant loss in performance. The process typically involves training the student to mimic the outputs or internal representations of the teacher. Beyond its primary application in creating lightweight models, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile framework used to enhance model generalization, transfer knowledge across different architectures, and enable advanced learning strategies.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm where a compact "student" model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This process facilitates the deployment of powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by reducing their size and computational requirements. The technique has found wide application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, for tasks ranging from text generation to image classification. The core principle involves transferring the knowledge embedded in the teacher's outputs or internal representations to the student. Advanced variations of this technique have emerged, such as data-free distillation for scenarios with private data, self-distillation where a model learns from itself, and ensemble distillation using multiple teachers. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation can also be used to improve a model's performance, transfer specific capabilities like adversarial robustness, and create more efficient and generalizable models.
