papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Learning Perception-Aware Agile Flight in Cluttered Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, neural control policies have outperformed existing model-based planning-and-control methods for autonomously navigating quadrotors through cluttered environments in minimum time. However, they are not perception aware, a crucial requirement in vision-based navigation due to the camera's limited field of view and the underactuated nature of a quadrotor. We propose a learning-based system that achieves perception-aware, agile flight in cluttered environments. Our method combines imitation learning with reinforcement learning (RL) by leveraging a privileged learning-by-cheating framework. Using RL, we first train a perception-aware teacher policy with full-state information to fly in minimum time through cluttered environments. Then, we use imitation learning to distill its knowledge into a vision-based student policy that only perceives the environment via a camera. Our approach tightly couples perception and control, showing a significant advantage in computation speed (10 times faster) and success rate. We demonstrate the closed-loop control performance using hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prevalent model compression technique used to create smaller, more efficient "student" neural networks that learn from larger, more complex "teacher" models. This process transfers the knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student to achieve high performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost. The applications of this technique are broad, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and graph-based machine learning. Methods range from mimicking the teacher's output predictions to more advanced techniques like imitating intermediate feature representations. Researchers have also developed specialized distillation strategies for complex tasks, data-scarce scenarios, and for transferring properties like adversarial robustness, making it a versatile tool for deploying state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models, particularly in natural language processing, pose significant challenges for their deployment in resource-constrained or latency-sensitive environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent model compression technique to address these issues. This method involves transferring knowledge from a large, cumbersome "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. Various advanced strategies have been developed to enhance this process, including using multiple teachers, employing adversarial learning, and enabling the teacher to learn how to teach via meta-learning. The applications of knowledge distillation are diverse, extending from compressing large language models and enabling efficient graph-based inference to facilitating federated learning across heterogeneous devices. These techniques allow for the creation of smaller, faster models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making state-of-the-art deep learning more accessible for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Approach for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the "teacher," to a smaller, more efficient model, the "student." The primary objective is to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. This process enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices and edge computing systems. The technique has found wide-ranging applications across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and healthcare, demonstrating its flexibility in creating models that are not only smaller and faster but also sometimes more interpretable or robust.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and computational cost of modern deep learning models pose significant challenges for their deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent and effective model compression technique to address this issue. The method operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve high performance with a fraction of the computational resources. Beyond its primary use in creating smaller and faster models, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile framework with applications in improving model generalization, enabling knowledge transfer in data-private scenarios, and adapting models to new domains.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Enhancement in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning where a compact "student" model is trained to mimic a larger, more complex "teacher" model. The primary goal is to create smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. This is achieved by transferring the rich knowledge embedded in the teacher's outputs or internal feature representations to the student. The applications of this versatile framework are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. Beyond simply reducing model size, knowledge distillation is also used to enhance student model performance, improve generalization, and address challenges such as data privacy and algorithmic fairness.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, called the 'student'. This process enables the creation of compact neural networks that are suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. The core idea is to train the student model to mimic the output distribution of the teacher model, leveraging the rich, learned information contained in the teacher's predictions. Variations of this technique include using multiple teachers, distilling knowledge from intermediate feature layers, and even training teacher models to be more 'student-friendly'. Knowledge distillation has found wide application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, as well as in specialized paradigms like federated learning to preserve privacy and improve communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the deployment of large, complex models in resource-constrained environments. The core idea involves transferring knowledge from a large, pre-trained 'teacher' model to a smaller 'student' model, enabling the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost. Beyond simple compression, this paradigm has been adapted to address a wide range of challenges. Researchers have successfully employed knowledge distillation to enhance model fairness by mitigating algorithmic and gender biases, to improve data privacy by creating models with differential privacy guarantees, and even to develop student models that outperform their teachers. This adaptability across various domains, including natural language processing and graph-based learning, highlights knowledge distillation as a powerful and flexible tool in the development of efficient and responsible AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: More Than Just Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning, primarily known for model compression. It involves transferring knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, the 'student'. While the initial goal was to reduce the computational and memory footprint of models for deployment on resource-constrained devices, the application and understanding of knowledge distillation have significantly evolved. Modern approaches now leverage distillation not only for compression but also to enhance student model performance, enable training in data-scarce or private environments, and improve the robustness of learning. Advanced methods distill information from intermediate layers, attention mechanisms, and even from the student model itself in a process called self-distillation. This demonstrates that knowledge distillation is a versatile and fundamental framework for optimizing and improving deep learning models across a wide range of tasks and constraints.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large, complex deep learning models into smaller, more efficient counterparts. This process involves a "teacher-student" paradigm, where a smaller student network learns to mimic the outputs or internal representations of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student model can achieve comparable performance while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. This makes it possible to deploy state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, such as on mobile devices or for latency-sensitive applications. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing, where it is used to create compact language models, and computer vision, for tasks like object detection and image classification. Research continues to explore novel distillation methods, including data-free approaches and cross-architecture knowledge transfer, further enhancing its flexibility and effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: The Versatility of Knowledge Distillation in Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning, primarily known for model compression. It enables the creation of smaller, more efficient 'student' models by transferring knowledge from larger, more complex 'teacher' models. This process is critical for deploying state-of-the-art networks in resource-constrained environments. However, the utility of knowledge distillation extends far beyond simple compression. Its applications now encompass a wide range of objectives, including enhancing model interpretability, promoting algorithmic fairness, preserving data privacy in distributed learning settings, and unifying knowledge from multiple disparate models. While the process is not without its challenges, such as the potential for propagating teacher model errors, its flexibility across diverse domains like natural language processing and computer vision makes it a foundational and versatile tool for developing efficient, effective, and responsible artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique in deep learning for model compression and performance enhancement. Operating on a teacher-student framework, it enables the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex model to a smaller, more efficient one. The primary objective is to create compact yet powerful models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without significant performance degradation. This versatile approach has found wide-ranging applications in natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition. Its utility extends beyond mere compression, serving to improve model generalization, enable privacy-preserving distributed learning, and even allow student models to surpass their teachers in performance.

papers_seen.author: Murillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. This process enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. The technique involves training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs, often using its softened probability distributions or intermediate feature representations. Its applications are wide-ranging, spanning domains like natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful machine learning technique where a compact 'student' model learns from a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process enables the creation of smaller, faster, and more computationally efficient neural networks that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts. Initially conceived for model compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now widely used across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, to adapt large models for specific tasks, improve model robustness against adversarial attacks, and facilitate learning across different data modalities. By transferring learned representations rather than just final predictions, this framework provides a flexible and effective method for deploying state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning for model compression and knowledge transfer. The core concept involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This process allows for the deployment of complex neural networks on resource-constrained devices by creating lightweight versions without a significant drop in accuracy. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation is also used to enhance model performance, transfer capabilities across different model architectures or data modalities, and address challenges such as privacy in federated learning and adversarial robustness. Its applications are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and graph-based learning.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for model compression, enabling the creation of smaller, more efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger, cumbersome teacher models. This process allows for the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has emerged as a versatile framework that can also enhance a model's generalization capabilities, improve its robustness against adversarial attacks, and increase its interpretability. By leveraging the rich information contained in a teacher's predictions, this technique offers a multifaceted approach to optimizing neural networks for a wide range of practical applications in natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Robust and Resource-Efficient Data-Free Knowledge Distillation by Generative Pseudo Replay
papers_seen.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows knowledge transfer from a trained neural network (teacher) to a more compact one (student) in the absence of original training data. Existing works use a validation set to monitor the accuracy of the student over real data and report the highest performance throughout the entire process. However, validation data may not be available at distillation time either, making it infeasible to record the student snapshot that achieved the peak accuracy. Therefore, a practical data-free KD method should be robust and ideally provide monotonically increasing student accuracy during distillation. This is challenging because the student experiences knowledge degradation due to the distribution shift of the synthetic data. A straightforward approach to overcome this issue is to store and rehearse the generated samples periodically, which increases the memory footprint and creates privacy concerns. We propose to model the distribution of the previously observed synthetic samples with a generative network. In particular, we design a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a training objective that is customized to learn the synthetic data representations optimally. The student is rehearsed by the generative pseudo replay technique, with samples produced by the VAE. Hence knowledge degradation can be prevented without storing any samples. Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that our method optimizes the expected value of the distilled model accuracy while eliminating the large memory overhead incurred by the sample-storing methods.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models have achieved unprecedented performance but their immense size and computational cost often hinder practical deployment. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression framework to address this challenge. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer resources. This makes it possible to deploy state-of-the-art models on devices with limited computational power, such as mobile phones. The technique's versatility is demonstrated by its broad application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and its adaptation into advanced methods like self-distillation and data-free distillation, further expanding its utility in developing efficient and robust AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique in deep learning, primarily known for model compression. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, cumbersome 'teacher' model, making it feasible to deploy state-of-the-art architectures on resource-constrained devices. However, the applications of knowledge distillation extend far beyond mere compression. It serves as a flexible framework for transferring knowledge to enhance model accuracy, enable continuous learning across sequential tasks, facilitate domain adaptation without source data, and even improve performance in multi-task learning settings. This versatility makes knowledge distillation a critical tool for advancing the practical application and capabilities of modern neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Paradigm for Efficient and Adaptable Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient counterparts. This process, where a compact "student" model learns from a larger "teacher" model, is crucial for deploying state-of-the-art neural networks on resource-constrained devices. Beyond simple compression, distillation has evolved into a versatile framework for transferring knowledge in a variety of challenging contexts. It enables training without access to original data, facilitates collaborative learning across heterogeneous devices in federated settings, and improves model generalization and adaptation to new domains. This demonstrates that knowledge distillation is not merely a compression tool but a fundamental paradigm for making advanced artificial intelligence more practical, private, and widely applicable.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large, state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This process involves training a smaller 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The core principle is to transfer the nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, often encapsulated in its soft predictions, to the more compact student network. This approach has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, to compress models like large language transformers and generative adversarial networks. Advanced methods have been developed that utilize multiple teachers, distill knowledge from intermediate layers, and even operate in data-free settings to address privacy concerns. Furthermore, knowledge distillation plays a crucial role in communication-efficient frameworks like federated learning, demonstrating its versatility and importance in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Compressing Deep Learning Models for Enhanced Efficiency
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning and natural language processing. It facilitates the creation of compact, efficient 'student' models by transferring knowledge from larger, more complex 'teacher' models. This process allows for the deployment of powerful neural networks on devices with limited computational and storage resources, such as mobile phones. Various distillation strategies have been developed, including methods that function without access to the original training data, thereby addressing privacy and data availability concerns. By mimicking the outputs or intermediate representations of a teacher model, the student network can achieve comparable performance with a significantly smaller footprint, making it a versatile tool for optimizing deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for model compression and performance optimization in deep learning. It involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student to achieve comparable or even superior performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost. Various strategies have been developed, including distilling knowledge from the teacher's final outputs, internal feature representations, or an ensemble of multiple teachers. This methodology has been successfully applied across a wide range of domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and federated learning, to create compact, fast, and effective models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Technique for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique for model compression within deep learning. This process operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of complex neural networks, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. Beyond simple compression, research has shown that knowledge distillation can also enhance the performance of student models. Its applications are broad, spanning critical domains like natural language processing and computer vision, demonstrating its importance in making advanced AI systems more practical and accessible.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and computational cost of modern deep learning models pose significant challenges for their deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent and effective model compression technique to address this issue. The method operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve high performance with a fraction of the computational resources. Beyond its primary use in creating smaller and faster models, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile framework with applications in improving model generalization, enabling knowledge transfer in data-private scenarios, and adapting models to new domains.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The primary objective is to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. This is achieved by training the student to mimic the teacher's behavior, often by replicating its output probabilities or internal feature representations. The applications of this versatile framework are broad, spanning domains such as natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition, where it is used not only for compression but also to enhance model performance, improve interpretability, and facilitate privacy-preserving learning.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions suitable for real-world deployment. Originally conceived for model compression, its applications have expanded significantly across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. Research shows that distillation not only reduces model size and inference time but can also enhance the student model's performance, sometimes even surpassing models trained from scratch. Advanced methods like self-distillation and data-free distillation further broaden its utility, making it a crucial tool for developing practical and effective deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex teacher model to a smaller, more efficient student model. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a significant loss in performance. This is typically achieved by training the student to mimic the outputs or internal representations of the teacher. Over time, techniques have evolved beyond simple output matching to include methods based on intermediate features, attention mechanisms, and adversarial learning. These advanced approaches have demonstrated success across a wide range of tasks and domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and generative modeling, making knowledge distillation a critical tool for operationalizing state-of-the-art deep learning models.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models, particularly in natural language processing, pose significant challenges for their deployment in resource-constrained or latency-sensitive environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent model compression technique to address these issues. This method involves transferring knowledge from a large, cumbersome "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. Various advanced strategies have been developed to enhance this process, including using multiple teachers, employing adversarial learning, and enabling the teacher to learn how to teach via meta-learning. The applications of knowledge distillation are diverse, extending from compressing large language models and enabling efficient graph-based inference to facilitating federated learning across heterogeneous devices. These techniques allow for the creation of smaller, faster models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making state-of-the-art deep learning more accessible for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Cruz

This enables the deployment of complex neural networks on devices with limited computational resources. Knowledge is typically transferred by training the student on the teacher's output probabilities or its internal feature representations. While its primary use is model compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness against adversarial attacks, and transferring knowledge in data-scarce or privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique designed to train a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to emulate the performance of a larger, high-capacity 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to reduce computational and memory requirements for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in accuracy. This process involves transferring knowledge from the teacher to the student, often using the teacher's output probabilities as soft labels. Researchers have developed various methods to address challenges such as the unavailability of original training data, leading to data-free and zero-shot distillation techniques. Other advanced strategies include distilling knowledge from an ensemble of teachers into a single student, using adversarial learning to guide the process, and adapting the technique for multi-task learning and specialized domains like computer vision and natural language processing. These approaches aim to create compact models that are not only efficient but also robust and comparable in performance to their larger counterparts.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning for transferring knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process serves a dual purpose: it facilitates model compression, enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices, and it often enhances the performance and generalization capabilities of the student model beyond what could be achieved through standard training. Its applications are broad, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, proving to be a flexible and powerful tool for optimizing deep neural networks for practical use.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary objective is to reduce computational and memory requirements for inference, enabling the deployment of powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments, while preserving high performance. This is achieved by training the student to mimic the teacher's behavior, often using its output probabilities as supervisory signals. The technique has found wide application across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, leading to numerous advancements and specialized methods to improve the knowledge transfer process.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly large language and vision models, have achieved state-of-the-art performance but are often computationally expensive and memory-intensive, hindering their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Model compression techniques address this challenge by creating smaller, more efficient models without significant performance degradation. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible method for this purpose. This process involves training a compact "student" network to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" network. By transferring the rich "dark knowledge" from the teacher, such as class relationship information or intermediate feature representations, the student model can achieve performance comparable to its larger counterpart. This approach has proven effective across a wide range of applications, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, demonstrating its versatility in making advanced AI more accessible and practical.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Distilling Object Detectors with Fine-grained Feature Imitation
papers_seen.abstract: State-of-the-art CNN based recognition models are often computationally prohibitive to deploy on low-end devices. A promising high level approach tackling this limitation is knowledge distillation, which let small student model mimic cumbersome teacher model's output to get improved generalization. However, related methods mainly focus on simple task of classification while do not consider complex tasks like object detection. We show applying the vanilla knowledge distillation to detection model gets minor gain. To address the challenge of distilling knowledge in detection model, we propose a fine-grained feature imitation method exploiting the cross-location discrepancy of feature response. Our intuition is that detectors care more about local near object regions. Thus the discrepancy of feature response on the near object anchor locations reveals important information of how teacher model tends to generalize. We design a novel mechanism to estimate those locations and let student model imitate the teacher on them to get enhanced performance. We first validate the idea on a developed lightweight toy detector which carries simplest notion of current state-of-the-art anchor based detection models on challenging KITTI dataset, our method generates up to 15% boost of mAP for the student model compared to the non-imitated counterpart. We then extensively evaluate the method with Faster R-CNN model under various scenarios with common object detection benchmark of Pascal VOC and COCO, imitation alleviates up to 74% performance drop of student model compared to teacher. Codes released at https://github.com/twangnh/Distilling-Object-Detectors

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models have achieved unprecedented performance but their immense size and computational cost often hinder practical deployment. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression framework to address this challenge. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer resources. This makes it possible to deploy state-of-the-art models on devices with limited computational power, such as mobile phones. The technique's versatility is demonstrated by its broad application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and its adaptation into advanced methods like self-distillation and data-free distillation, further expanding its utility in developing efficient and robust AI systems.
