papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful machine learning technique where a compact 'student' model learns from a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process enables the creation of smaller, faster, and more computationally efficient neural networks that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts. Initially conceived for model compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now widely used across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, to adapt large models for specific tasks, improve model robustness against adversarial attacks, and facilitate learning across different data modalities. By transferring learned representations rather than just final predictions, this framework provides a flexible and effective method for deploying state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression paradigm where a compact 'student' model learns from a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This technique aims to create smaller, more efficient networks that retain the high performance of their cumbersome counterparts, making them suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Initially focused on mimicking output probabilities, the field has evolved to encompass a wide range of applications beyond simple classification, including complex tasks in natural language processing and computer vision. The effectiveness of distillation is now understood to hinge on more sophisticated methods, such as transferring knowledge from internal feature representations and adapting the process to transfer specific qualities like adversarial robustness. Modern approaches integrate distillation with other compression techniques and advanced training strategies, demonstrating its versatility and importance in developing state-of-the-art, deployable deep learning models.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, such as mobile phones, without a significant loss in accuracy. The student model learns from the rich information contained in the teacher's outputs, including class probabilities and intermediate feature representations. This technique has found broad applications across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, not only for creating smaller and faster models but also for improving model robustness, generalization, and interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Murillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary goal is to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. This process enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. The technique involves training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs, often using its softened probability distributions or intermediate feature representations. Its applications are wide-ranging, spanning domains like natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient ones. This process involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a pre-trained, cumbersome 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to retain the high performance of the teacher model while significantly reducing computational and storage costs, making advanced models deployable on resource-constrained devices. The applications of knowledge distillation are broad, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and healthcare. Beyond simple output matching, advanced methods focus on transferring knowledge from intermediate feature representations and using adversarial techniques to improve the student's learning process. This versatility makes knowledge distillation a crucial tool for optimizing and deploying state-of-the-art neural networks in real-world scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Paradigm for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Originally conceived as a method for a smaller "student" model to learn from a larger "teacher" model, the paradigm has evolved significantly. Research now shows that the benefits of distillation extend beyond simple mimicry, with the regularization effects of soft labels playing a crucial role. This technique has proven effective in a wide array of complex domains, including natural language processing for text generation and translation, the compression of generative adversarial networks, and the optimization of graph neural networks. Advanced methods such as self-distillation, adversarial training, and extensions for domain adaptation further highlight its versatility. Ultimately, knowledge distillation is a critical tool for creating efficient, yet powerful, AI systems suitable for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective model compression technique that transfers knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. The core idea involves training the student network to mimic the outputs or internal representations of the teacher. Innovations in this field have expanded the technique's applicability, leading to methods like zero-shot distillation, which functions without access to the original training data, and self-distillation, where a model learns from its own representations. These approaches have been successfully applied to compress a wide range of models, from large-scale language models in Natural Language Processing (NLP) to complex architectures used in computer vision and multimodal tasks, demonstrating the flexibility and practical utility of knowledge distillation in creating lightweight, yet powerful, AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly large-scale language models in Natural Language Processing (NLP), have achieved state-of-the-art performance but are often too large and slow for practical deployment. Model compression techniques are essential for creating smaller, more efficient models. Knowledge distillation is a popular compression paradigm where a compact "student" model learns from a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This process involves transferring the teacher's knowledge, often through its output probabilities or internal representations, to guide the student's training. Advanced methods have emerged, including multi-teacher distillation, self-distillation, and data-free approaches that work without the original training data. Knowledge distillation can also be combined with other compression methods like pruning and quantization to further enhance model efficiency, making powerful deep learning models accessible for resource-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. This process enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. By training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs, including the nuanced probability distributions over classes, the student model can achieve performance far superior to what it could by training on the ground-truth labels alone. This method has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts while being significantly faster and smaller.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: DINE: Domain Adaptation from Single and Multiple Black-box Predictors
papers_seen.abstract: To ease the burden of labeling, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to transfer knowledge in previous and related labeled datasets (sources) to a new unlabeled dataset (target). Despite impressive progress, prior methods always need to access the raw source data and develop data-dependent alignment approaches to recognize the target samples in a transductive learning manner, which may raise privacy concerns from source individuals. Several recent studies resort to an alternative solution by exploiting the well-trained white-box model from the source domain, yet, it may still leak the raw data through generative adversarial learning. This paper studies a practical and interesting setting for UDA, where only black-box source models (i.e., only network predictions are available) are provided during adaptation in the target domain. To solve this problem, we propose a new two-step knowledge adaptation framework called DIstill and fine-tuNE (DINE). Taking into consideration the target data structure, DINE first distills the knowledge from the source predictor to a customized target model, then fine-tunes the distilled model to further fit the target domain. Besides, neural networks are not required to be identical across domains in DINE, even allowing effective adaptation on a low-resource device. Empirical results on three UDA scenarios (i.e., single-source, multi-source, and partial-set) confirm that DINE achieves highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art data-dependent approaches. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/tim-learn/DINE/}.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: From Model Compression to a Versatile Deep Learning Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning, initially developed for model compression. It enables the creation of small, efficient "student" models by transferring knowledge from large, complex "teacher" models, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. While its primary use is to reduce computational and memory footprints, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It has evolved into a versatile framework used not only for creating compact models but also for enhancing model performance, improving interpretability, and enabling novel forms of knowledge transfer across different domains, modalities, and architectures. This demonstrates its crucial role in developing more practical, robust, and capable artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Effective Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: As deep learning models grow in size and complexity, their deployment in resource-constrained environments becomes a significant challenge. Model compression techniques are essential for creating smaller, faster, and more efficient models without substantial performance degradation. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for this purpose. It involves transferring knowledge from a large, cumbersome 'teacher' model to a smaller 'student' model. The student learns to mimic the rich output distributions of the teacher, thereby inheriting its performance capabilities while maintaining a much smaller footprint. This approach has proven effective across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, enabling the use of state-of-the-art architectures in practical, real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique for model compression in deep learning. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to create compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, such as mobile phones, without a significant loss in accuracy. While originally conceived for reducing model size and inference time, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now used not only for creating smaller and faster models but also for enhancing model performance, improving interpretability, and addressing practical challenges like data privacy. This demonstrates its evolution from a simple compression tool into a multifaceted framework for developing more efficient, robust, and practical artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Deleon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a key model compression technique to address this issue. In this paradigm, a smaller 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model, effectively transferring its learned knowledge. This process enables the creation of lightweight yet powerful models that are faster and more efficient at inference. Beyond simple size reduction, knowledge distillation has demonstrated the ability to enhance student model performance, improve robustness, and mitigate undesirable biases. As a flexible and multifaceted framework, it serves as a crucial tool for making state-of-the-art deep learning models practical for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Effective Strategy for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques have emerged as a critical field of study to address these issues. Knowledge distillation, a prominent compression method, involves training a smaller 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student model to achieve performance far exceeding what it could attain by training on ground-truth labels alone. This approach has proven versatile, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, leading to models that are not only smaller and faster but also maintain high levels of accuracy, facilitating the practical application of state-of-the-art deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful paradigm in deep learning where a compact student model is trained to reproduce the behavior of a larger, more complex teacher model. Originally conceived for model compression, this technique enables the deployment of powerful neural networks on resource-constrained devices by creating smaller, faster versions without a significant loss in performance. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation has proven to be a versatile framework with applications in domain adaptation, lifelong learning, privacy preservation, and improving the generalization capabilities of models. By transferring nuanced knowledge from the teacher, such as class relationship probabilities and internal feature representations, the student model can often achieve better performance and robustness than if it were trained on ground-truth labels alone.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a large, pre-trained model to a more compact one. This teacher-student paradigm is primarily used for model compression, enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art architectures on resource-constrained devices. However, its utility extends significantly beyond this initial purpose. The method has been successfully adapted to enhance model performance, improve generalization, and address critical concerns such as data privacy, algorithmic fairness, and model interpretability. Its flexibility across diverse domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, establishes knowledge distillation as a foundational tool for developing practical, efficient, and responsible artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique that facilitates the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. This is achieved by training the student to mimic the outputs or internal representations of the teacher. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. Advanced methods have been developed to address specific challenges, such as transferring adversarial robustness, performing distillation without access to original training data, mitigating biases, and improving the interaction between teacher and student models.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression paradigm where a compact "student" network learns from a larger "teacher" network. This technique facilitates the deployment of complex deep learning models in settings with limited computational resources. The process involves transferring knowledge through various mechanisms, including mimicking the teacher's final outputs, aligning intermediate feature representations, or preserving relational knowledge. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse fields such as natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition. Beyond simple compression, this framework can be used for more advanced purposes, including transferring specific properties like adversarial robustness or inductive biases between different model architectures. It also enables novel applications like cross-modal learning and improving models in federated learning environments.

papers_seen.author: Robbins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance but are often too large and computationally expensive for practical deployment. Knowledge distillation addresses this challenge by enabling the creation of smaller, more efficient models. This process involves a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact student model learns to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge from the teacher, the student can achieve comparable or even superior performance with a significantly smaller footprint. This technique has proven highly adaptable, with successful applications in natural language processing and computer vision, bridging the gap between cutting-edge research and deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression paradigm where a compact "student" network learns from a larger "teacher" network. This technique facilitates the deployment of complex deep learning models in settings with limited computational resources. The process involves transferring knowledge through various mechanisms, including mimicking the teacher's final outputs, aligning intermediate feature representations, or preserving relational knowledge. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse fields such as natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition. Beyond simple compression, this framework can be used for more advanced purposes, including transferring specific properties like adversarial robustness or inductive biases between different model architectures. It also enables novel applications like cross-modal learning and improving models in federated learning environments.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large, complex deep learning models into smaller, more efficient counterparts. This process involves a "teacher-student" paradigm, where a smaller student network learns to mimic the outputs or internal representations of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student model can achieve comparable performance while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. This makes it possible to deploy state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, such as on mobile devices or for latency-sensitive applications. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing, where it is used to create compact language models, and computer vision, for tasks like object detection and image classification. Research continues to explore novel distillation methods, including data-free approaches and cross-architecture knowledge transfer, further enhancing its flexibility and effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale deep learning models, particularly in natural language processing, have demonstrated state-of-the-art performance but are often too large and computationally expensive for real-world applications. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent model compression technique to address this challenge. This method involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model, thereby transferring its learned knowledge. This process allows for the creation of smaller, faster models that maintain high performance, making them suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Advanced approaches have extended this framework to scenarios without original training data, settings with multiple teachers, and decentralized paradigms like federated learning, showcasing its versatility and importance in creating efficient AI systems.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Wide Neural Networks: Risk Bound, Data Efficiency and Imperfect Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a strategy of training a student network with guide of the soft output from a teacher network. It has been a successful method of model compression and knowledge transfer. However, currently knowledge distillation lacks a convincing theoretical understanding. On the other hand, recent finding on neural tangent kernel enables us to approximate a wide neural network with a linear model of the network's random features. In this paper, we theoretically analyze the knowledge distillation of a wide neural network. First we provide a transfer risk bound for the linearized model of the network. Then we propose a metric of the task's training difficulty, called data inefficiency. Based on this metric, we show that for a perfect teacher, a high ratio of teacher's soft labels can be beneficial. Finally, for the case of imperfect teacher, we find that hard labels can correct teacher's wrong prediction, which explains the practice of mixing hard and soft labels.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the deployment of powerful models in resource-constrained environments. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve comparable or even superior performance with significantly lower computational and memory costs. While initially conceived for compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now used across diverse domains like natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning not only to create smaller models but also to enhance performance, improve robustness against adversarial attacks, and transfer specialized knowledge, demonstrating its versatility as a fundamental tool in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Crosby
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful and versatile model compression technique in deep learning. It employs a teacher-student framework where a smaller, computationally efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and predictions of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the nuanced knowledge from the teacher, the student can achieve comparable or even enhanced performance while having a significantly smaller footprint. This process enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices, bridging the gap between high accuracy and practical applicability in fields like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression and Optimization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm wherein a compact "student" model is trained to reproduce the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. The primary objective is to transfer the generalized knowledge from the cumbersome teacher to the lightweight student, thereby creating a smaller, faster model suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. This technique has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. By learning from the richer, soft probability distributions output by the teacher, rather than just the hard labels from the training data, the student model can often achieve performance superior to what it could attain if trained on the data alone.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework Beyond Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a foundational technique in deep learning, initially developed for model compression. This process involves training a compact 'student' model to replicate the behavior of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model, facilitating the deployment of advanced architectures in resource-constrained environments. However, the utility of this framework extends far beyond simply reducing model size. Knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile tool for enhancing model performance, transferring desirable properties such as adversarial robustness, and improving the interpretability of opaque 'black-box' models. Through advanced methods like self-distillation and applications in privacy-sensitive domains, it has become a critical component for developing more efficient, effective, and trustworthy AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has produced increasingly large and complex models that achieve state-of-the-art performance but are often impractical for deployment due to their computational and memory requirements. Model compression techniques, particularly knowledge distillation, address this challenge by transferring knowledge from a large, cumbersome 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process enables the creation of compact models that retain a significant portion of the teacher's performance, making them suitable for resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. The flexibility of knowledge distillation is evident in its successful application across various domains, including natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph-based learning, as well as its adaptability to scenarios where the original training data is unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance in many fields, but their large size and computational demands often prevent their use in resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques address this issue, with knowledge distillation emerging as a prominent and versatile paradigm. This method involves a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The process transfers the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher to the student, enabling the creation of compact models that are faster and require less memory. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation can also enhance the performance and generalization of the student model, making it a powerful tool for optimizing neural networks for practical deployment.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that addresses the challenge of deploying large, complex models in resource-constrained environments. The process involves a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This knowledge transfer allows the student to achieve high accuracy without the computational overhead of the teacher. The versatility of this framework has led to its successful application across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making it a critical tool for developing practical and accessible artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Koch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prevalent model compression technique designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The primary goal is to reduce computational and memory requirements for deployment while maintaining high performance. This process is achieved through various methods, including mimicking the teacher's output predictions, intermediate feature representations, or latent knowledge structures. Research in this area has expanded to address advanced scenarios such as handling exceptionally strong teachers, training teachers to be more effective for distillation, and performing distillation without access to the original training data. Knowledge distillation has proven to be a versatile and effective technique, with successful applications across diverse fields including natural language processing, computer vision, recommender systems, and medical imaging.

papers_seen.author: Deleon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a key model compression technique to address this issue. In this paradigm, a smaller 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model, effectively transferring its learned knowledge. This process enables the creation of lightweight yet powerful models that are faster and more efficient at inference. Beyond simple size reduction, knowledge distillation has demonstrated the ability to enhance student model performance, improve robustness, and mitigate undesirable biases. As a flexible and multifaceted framework, it serves as a crucial tool for making state-of-the-art deep learning models practical for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: From Model Compression to a Versatile Deep Learning Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning, initially developed for model compression. It enables the creation of small, efficient "student" models by transferring knowledge from large, complex "teacher" models, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. While its primary use is to reduce computational and memory footprints, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It has evolved into a versatile framework used not only for creating compact models but also for enhancing model performance, improving interpretability, and enabling novel forms of knowledge transfer across different domains, modalities, and architectures. This demonstrates its crucial role in developing more practical, robust, and capable artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous domains, but their large size and computational expense often hinder deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and effective model compression technique to address this challenge. The process involves a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge embedded in the teacher's predictions or internal representations, the student can achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer parameters. The utility of this framework has expanded beyond simple compression, proving effective for enhancing model performance, transferring specific capabilities like adversarial robustness, and even mitigating societal biases within language models. Advanced methods such as self-distillation, online distillation, and data-free approaches further increase its versatility, making it a critical tool for developing efficient and practical AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: More Than Just Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile technique in deep learning designed to compress large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions. This process involves a compact 'student' model being trained to mimic the behavior of a pre-trained, cumbersome 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to retain the high performance of the teacher while reducing computational and memory requirements, enabling the deployment of advanced models on resource-constrained devices. However, the applications and implications of knowledge distillation extend far beyond simple compression. It serves as a powerful framework for knowledge transfer, performance enhancement, and addressing ethical considerations like fairness, making it a fundamental tool for creating more practical and robust artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous tasks, but their large size and computational expense often hinder their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. This method involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model, effectively transferring the teacher's learned knowledge. This process allows for the creation of compact models that are significantly faster and smaller, yet retain a high level of performance. Knowledge distillation has proven to be a flexible and effective strategy across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, enabling the development of powerful and practical AI applications.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and powerful technique for model compression within the field of deep learning. This paradigm addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from a large 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The student is trained to mimic the behavior of the teacher, often by learning from its softened probability outputs or intermediate feature representations. This process allows the compact student model to achieve high performance, often comparable to its much larger teacher, without the associated computational and memory overhead. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated by its successful application across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making it an essential tool for developing practical and deployable AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning designed to compress large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions. The process involves training a compact "student" model to mimic the behavior and outputs of a pre-trained, high-performance "teacher" model. This knowledge transfer enables the deployment of powerful artificial intelligence systems in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a substantial loss in accuracy. While originally conceived for model compression, the applications of distillation have expanded significantly, now serving as a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling advanced learning paradigms like domain adaptation and federated learning.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm where a compact "student" model is trained to reproduce the performance of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This technique addresses the challenge of deploying computationally intensive deep learning networks on resource-constrained devices. The process involves transferring knowledge from the teacher to the student, often by using the teacher's output probabilities as soft labels or by mimicking its internal feature representations. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing for tasks like machine translation and language model compression, and in computer vision for object detection and image generation. Advanced applications of this framework include enhancing model robustness, preserving privacy in federated learning, and enabling data-free model training.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for model compression and performance optimization in deep learning. It involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student to achieve comparable or even superior performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost. Various strategies have been developed, including distilling knowledge from the teacher's final outputs, internal feature representations, or an ensemble of multiple teachers. This methodology has been successfully applied across a wide range of domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and federated learning, to create compact, fast, and effective models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient ones. This process involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a pre-trained, cumbersome 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to retain the high performance of the teacher model while significantly reducing computational and storage costs, making advanced models deployable on resource-constrained devices. The applications of knowledge distillation are broad, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and healthcare. Beyond simple output matching, advanced methods focus on transferring knowledge from intermediate feature representations and using adversarial techniques to improve the student's learning process. This versatility makes knowledge distillation a crucial tool for optimizing and deploying state-of-the-art neural networks in real-world scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: From Model Compression to a Versatile Deep Learning Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a key technique in deep learning, initially developed for model compression. It involves a teacher-student paradigm where a compact "student" model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, more powerful "teacher" model. This process allows for the creation of smaller, faster models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. While its primary application is compression, the utility of knowledge distillation has expanded considerably. It is now used to enhance model performance, facilitate learning in data-scarce environments, and enable advanced paradigms like federated and lifelong learning, establishing it as a versatile framework for building more efficient and robust AI systems.
