papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Ibarra
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial and versatile technique for model compression in deep learning. This method employs a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary goal is to transfer the rich knowledge acquired by the teacher, enabling the student to achieve comparable performance while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. This process makes it feasible to deploy state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices, such as mobile phones. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing and computer vision, and its utility extends beyond simple compression to include performance enhancement and knowledge transfer in privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient neural networks. This is achieved through a teacher-student framework, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the outputs and internal representations of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of complex models, enabling their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation also serves as a versatile tool for enhancing the performance and interpretability of student models. The technique has been successfully applied across a wide array of domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, with ongoing research refining the methods for knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that addresses the challenge of deploying large, complex models in resource-constrained environments. The process involves a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This knowledge transfer allows the student to achieve high accuracy without the computational overhead of the teacher. The versatility of this framework has led to its successful application across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making it a critical tool for developing practical and accessible artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Model Compression and Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large, complex deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. This process typically involves a teacher-student framework, where a smaller student model learns to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This paradigm addresses the significant computational and storage costs associated with state-of-the-art models in fields like Natural Language Processing and computer vision. Various methods have been developed to tackle challenges such as data privacy, architectural mismatches between teacher and student, and information transfer efficiency. Applications are diverse, ranging from compressing large language models and generative adversarial networks to enhancing model robustness against adversarial attacks and enabling efficient federated learning. Extensions to the basic framework include using multiple teachers, adversarial learning, and data-free distillation techniques, continually expanding the utility of this compression strategy.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Murillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary goal is to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. This process enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. The technique involves training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs, often using its softened probability distributions or intermediate feature representations. Its applications are wide-ranging, spanning domains like natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Strategy for Compressing Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique where a compact "student" model learns to mimic the behavior of a larger, more complex "teacher" model. This process transfers the rich knowledge embedded in the teacher, enabling the creation of smaller, faster, and more efficient models without substantial performance degradation. By reducing computational and memory requirements, knowledge distillation facilitates the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning architectures on resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices and edge hardware. Its applications span numerous fields, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning, demonstrating its broad utility and effectiveness in making advanced AI more accessible and practical.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Effective Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: As deep learning models grow in size and complexity, their deployment in resource-constrained environments becomes a significant challenge. Model compression techniques are essential for creating smaller, faster, and more efficient models without substantial performance degradation. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for this purpose. It involves transferring knowledge from a large, cumbersome 'teacher' model to a smaller 'student' model. The student learns to mimic the rich output distributions of the teacher, thereby inheriting its performance capabilities while maintaining a much smaller footprint. This approach has proven effective across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, enabling the use of state-of-the-art architectures in practical, real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient and Practical Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous tasks but their significant computational and memory requirements pose major challenges for real-world deployment. Model compression techniques, particularly knowledge distillation, offer a powerful solution to this problem. Knowledge distillation is a training paradigm where a smaller "student" model learns to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This process allows the student to inherit the teacher's learned knowledge, resulting in a compact, efficient model that retains high performance. This approach has proven highly effective and adaptable, enabling the creation of practical models for diverse applications in natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and distributed learning systems, thereby bridging the gap between cutting-edge research and deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Feature-map-level Online Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Feature maps contain rich information about image intensity and spatial correlation. However, previous online knowledge distillation methods only utilize the class probabilities. Thus in this paper, we propose an online knowledge distillation method that transfers not only the knowledge of the class probabilities but also that of the feature map using the adversarial training framework. We train multiple networks simultaneously by employing discriminators to distinguish the feature map distributions of different networks. Each network has its corresponding discriminator which discriminates the feature map from its own as fake while classifying that of the other network as real. By training a network to fool the corresponding discriminator, it can learn the other network's feature map distribution. We show that our method performs better than the conventional direct alignment method such as L1 and is more suitable for online distillation. Also, we propose a novel cyclic learning scheme for training more than two networks together. We have applied our method to various network architectures on the classification task and discovered a significant improvement of performance especially in the case of training a pair of a small network and a large one.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The primary objective is to create compact models that retain the high performance of the teacher, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. This is typically achieved by training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs or internal feature representations. While initially conceived for compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. The framework is now used to enhance student model performance, sometimes even surpassing the teacher, and to address critical considerations like algorithmic fairness and data privacy. Its versatility has led to successful applications across diverse domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, establishing it as a multifaceted tool in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique for model compression in deep learning. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, enabling the creation of compact models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices, without a substantial loss in performance. This approach has proven effective and versatile, with broad applications across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, for both compressing models and enhancing their overall performance.

papers_seen.author: Frost
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile technique for compressing large, complex deep learning models into smaller, more efficient versions without a significant loss in performance. The process typically involves a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model that transfers its learned knowledge to a smaller 'student' model. By training the student to mimic the teacher's behavior, often through its output probabilities or intermediate feature representations, the smaller model can achieve high performance that would be unattainable by training on data alone. This approach is critical for deploying state-of-the-art models, particularly in natural language processing, on resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. The applications of knowledge distillation are broad, extending beyond simple compression to areas like domain adaptation, privacy preservation, and overall performance enhancement.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Paradigm for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Originally conceived as a method for a smaller "student" model to learn from a larger "teacher" model, the paradigm has evolved significantly. Research now shows that the benefits of distillation extend beyond simple mimicry, with the regularization effects of soft labels playing a crucial role. This technique has proven effective in a wide array of complex domains, including natural language processing for text generation and translation, the compression of generative adversarial networks, and the optimization of graph neural networks. Advanced methods such as self-distillation, adversarial training, and extensions for domain adaptation further highlight its versatility. Ultimately, knowledge distillation is a critical tool for creating efficient, yet powerful, AI systems suitable for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Task Enhancement in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning. This method involves training a compact "student" model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. Its primary application is to create lightweight, efficient models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. The utility of knowledge distillation extends across various domains, including natural language processing for compressing large language models and computer vision for tasks like object detection and generative modeling. Advanced strategies have also been developed, such as task-adaptive compression, data-free distillation, and online learning frameworks, showcasing the versatility and ongoing evolution of this technique.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models, particularly in natural language processing, pose significant challenges for their deployment in resource-constrained or latency-sensitive environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent model compression technique to address these issues. This method involves transferring knowledge from a large, cumbersome "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. Various advanced strategies have been developed to enhance this process, including using multiple teachers, employing adversarial learning, and enabling the teacher to learn how to teach via meta-learning. The applications of knowledge distillation are diverse, extending from compressing large language models and enabling efficient graph-based inference to facilitating federated learning across heterogeneous devices. These techniques allow for the creation of smaller, faster models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making state-of-the-art deep learning more accessible for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique in deep learning, primarily known for model compression. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, cumbersome 'teacher' model, making it feasible to deploy state-of-the-art architectures on resource-constrained devices. However, the applications of knowledge distillation extend far beyond mere compression. It serves as a flexible framework for transferring knowledge to enhance model accuracy, enable continuous learning across sequential tasks, facilitate domain adaptation without source data, and even improve performance in multi-task learning settings. This versatility makes knowledge distillation a critical tool for advancing the practical application and capabilities of modern neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Carney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Paradigm for Model Compression and Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning for model compression and knowledge transfer. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process allows for the creation of smaller, more efficient models that retain a significant portion of the original model's performance, making them suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Advances in this field have expanded its application beyond simple compression, with methods developed for distilling knowledge from intermediate features, ensembles of teachers, and even in scenarios where the original training data is unavailable. The versatility of knowledge distillation has led to its successful application in numerous areas, including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression paradigm in deep learning. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to replicate the performance of a larger, more complex teacher model. This process enables the deployment of powerful models on resource-constrained devices, which is critical for many real-world applications. The applications of knowledge distillation are diverse, spanning natural language processing tasks like language model compression and computer vision tasks such as compressing generative models. Researchers have developed numerous variations of the core technique, including methods that leverage multiple teachers, distill knowledge from intermediate network layers, and perform distillation without access to the original training data. Beyond creating smaller and faster models, knowledge distillation is also used to achieve other objectives, such as enhancing model privacy, improving interpretability, and mitigating biases.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for model compression in deep learning, addressing the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models in resource-constrained environments. This method involves a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers the rich knowledge from the teacher, enabling the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer resources. Beyond simple compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include enhancing model robustness, facilitating training without original data, and improving overall performance. Its adaptability across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, highlights its role as a foundational tool for creating practical and efficient AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Strategy for Compressing Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique where a compact "student" model learns to mimic the behavior of a larger, more complex "teacher" model. This process transfers the rich knowledge embedded in the teacher, enabling the creation of smaller, faster, and more efficient models without substantial performance degradation. By reducing computational and memory requirements, knowledge distillation facilitates the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning architectures on resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices and edge hardware. Its applications span numerous fields, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning, demonstrating its broad utility and effectiveness in making advanced AI more accessible and practical.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process enables the creation of compact neural networks suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. The student model is trained to mimic the behavior of the teacher, leveraging the rich, generalized information contained in its predictions or internal representations. While primarily used for reducing computational and memory footprints, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness, enabling domain adaptation, and facilitating privacy-preserving learning.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective model compression technique that transfers knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. The core idea involves training the student network to mimic the outputs or internal representations of the teacher. Innovations in this field have expanded the technique's applicability, leading to methods like zero-shot distillation, which functions without access to the original training data, and self-distillation, where a model learns from its own representations. These approaches have been successfully applied to compress a wide range of models, from large-scale language models in Natural Language Processing (NLP) to complex architectures used in computer vision and multimodal tasks, demonstrating the flexibility and practical utility of knowledge distillation in creating lightweight, yet powerful, AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Deep neural networks have become increasingly large and complex, which hinders their deployment on devices with limited computational resources. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. This method involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" network to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" network or an ensemble of models. The student learns to reproduce the teacher's outputs or its internal representations, effectively transferring the rich knowledge learned by the larger model. This process enables the creation of compact models that maintain high performance across a variety of domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning, without requiring architectural changes or additional data.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique designed to address the challenges of deploying large, computationally expensive deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. The process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior and replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the nuanced knowledge from the teacher, often encapsulated in its output probabilities or intermediate representations, the student model can achieve high performance with a significantly smaller footprint. This method has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, to create compact, fast, and efficient models suitable for practical, real-world applications on devices with limited computational power.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

Advanced approaches have extended this framework to scenarios without original training data, settings with multiple teachers, and decentralized paradigms like federated learning, showcasing its versatility and importance in creating efficient AI systems.

Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to overcome this challenge. The process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This technique is not limited to creating smaller models; its applications have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling complex learning paradigms, making it a versatile and fundamental tool in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Oliver

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique in deep learning for model compression and knowledge transfer. The student learns from the rich, generalized information encoded in the teacher's outputs, often achieving higher performance than if trained on ground-truth labels alone. Initially conceived for creating smaller and faster models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now a versatile framework used not only for compression but also to enhance model performance, robustness, and generalization across diverse domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Garrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and powerful technique in deep learning, primarily aimed at model compression. By transferring the nuanced knowledge from a teacher's internal representations or output probabilities, the student can achieve superior performance than by learning from data alone. The applications of this versatile framework extend beyond simple compression, proving effective in enhancing model robustness, transferring knowledge in data-scarce scenarios, and improving performance across a wide range of domains, including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

The primary goal is to reduce computational and memory requirements, enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. This versatile approach has proven effective across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and its applications extend beyond simple compression to performance enhancement and knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

Advanced methods leverage multiple teachers to improve knowledge transfer, and innovative approaches even permit distillation without access to the original training data. Furthermore, the technique can be adapted to various model architectures, including generative networks, and can be used to improve the interpretability of complex deep neural networks.

Beyond simple compression, distillation has evolved into a versatile framework for transferring knowledge in a variety of challenging contexts. It enables training without access to original data, facilitates collaborative learning across heterogeneous devices in federated settings, and improves model generalization and adaptation to new domains. This demonstrates that knowledge distillation is not merely a compression tool but a fundamental paradigm for making advanced artificial intelligence more practical, private, and widely applicable.

papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the "teacher," to a smaller, more efficient model, the "student." This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by reducing their size and inference latency without a significant loss in performance. The core idea involves training the student model to mimic the output distributions of the teacher model, effectively learning a richer, more generalized representation than it could from ground-truth labels alone. This technique has found broad applications across various domains, including Natural Language Processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. Research explores not only compressing models but also enhancing their performance, adapting them for multi-task learning, and enabling privacy-preserving or distributed learning paradigms.

papers_seen.author: West
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework Beyond Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a pivotal technique in deep learning, initially conceived as a method for model compression. This process involves transferring knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model, enabling the deployment of powerful neural networks in resource-constrained environments. However, the utility of knowledge distillation extends far beyond simple compression. It serves as a powerful framework for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and increasing the interpretability of opaque "black-box" models. By leveraging the rich, nuanced information captured by teacher models, knowledge distillation can guide student models to achieve superior accuracy, sometimes even surpassing their teachers, and can transform complex neural networks into simpler, more transparent structures like decision trees. This makes it a versatile and indispensable tool in the modern deep learning and natural language processing toolkit.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression and knowledge transfer technique in deep learning. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to replicate the performance of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in accuracy. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation can also be used to improve a model's performance, enhance its generalization capabilities across different data distributions, and transfer beneficial properties, such as inductive biases, from one model to another. The technique is versatile, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, and has given rise to numerous variations, including self-distillation, data-free distillation, and methods involving multiple or adaptive teachers.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The primary objective is to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. This is achieved by training the student to mimic the teacher's behavior, often by replicating its output probabilities or internal feature representations. The applications of this versatile framework are broad, spanning domains such as natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition, where it is used not only for compression but also to enhance model performance, improve interpretability, and facilitate privacy-preserving learning.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a significant loss in performance. The core idea involves training the student not only on the ground-truth data but also using the outputs or intermediate representations of the trained teacher as a richer, soft target. This method has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and recommender systems, leading to a wide range of lightweight models that retain the capabilities of their larger counterparts.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful machine learning technique focused on transferring knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the teacher, to a smaller, more efficient model, called the student. Originally conceived for model compression, this process allows for the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by creating smaller, faster versions that retain much of the original's performance. The applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly beyond simple compression. It is now used to improve the absolute performance of student models, sometimes even allowing them to outperform their teachers. Furthermore, the technique has been adapted to address challenges in diverse areas such as federated learning, data privacy, and multimodal learning. By leveraging the learned representations of a teacher, knowledge distillation provides a flexible framework for creating more practical, robust, and capable models across various domains, particularly in Natural Language Processing (NLP).

This is achieved by transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, often through its output probability distributions, to the student. It has proven effective across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for model compression and performance optimization in deep learning. It involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student to achieve comparable or even superior performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost. Various strategies have been developed, including distilling knowledge from the teacher's final outputs, internal feature representations, or an ensemble of multiple teachers. This methodology has been successfully applied across a wide range of domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and federated learning, to create compact, fast, and effective models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: From Model Compression to a Versatile Deep Learning Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a key technique in deep learning, initially developed for model compression. It involves a teacher-student paradigm where a compact "student" model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, more powerful "teacher" model. This process allows for the creation of smaller, faster models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. While its primary application is compression, the utility of knowledge distillation has expanded considerably. It is now used to enhance model performance, facilitate learning in data-scarce environments, and enable advanced paradigms like federated and lifelong learning, establishing it as a versatile framework for building more efficient and robust AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: The Versatility of Knowledge Distillation: From Model Compression to Advanced Learning Paradigms
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning, initially conceived for model compression. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. While its primary application is to create compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, the utility of knowledge distillation extends far beyond simple compression. It serves as a versatile framework for enhancing model accuracy, transferring knowledge across different tasks and data modalities, and enabling novel applications in areas such as federated learning and privacy-preserving machine learning. The evolution of this technique has led to sophisticated methods including multi-teacher learning, self-distillation, and cross-modal distillation, demonstrating its broad applicability and foundational role in developing efficient and robust AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Model Compression Technique in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression and knowledge transfer paradigm where a compact 'student' model learns from a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. This technique addresses the challenge of deploying large deep learning models, such as those used in natural language processing (NLP), on resource-constrained devices. By transferring knowledge from the teacher, often in the form of soft label probabilities, the student model can achieve performance comparable to its larger counterpart while being significantly smaller and faster. Various strategies have been developed, including data-free distillation, self-distillation, and multi-teacher approaches, extending its application to diverse tasks like machine translation, object detection, and question answering.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm where a smaller 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, more powerful 'teacher' model. This process enables the deployment of complex deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments by reducing their computational and memory footprints. The core principle involves transferring the generalized knowledge from the teacher to the student, often using the teacher's output probabilities as soft labels. The applications of this technique have expanded beyond simple compression to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling novel learning scenarios like data-free training and federated learning across heterogeneous devices.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved remarkable success but their large size and computational demands often prevent deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and knowledge of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers the rich, nuanced information learned by the teacher, allowing the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer resources. The utility of this technique extends beyond simple compression, with applications in enhancing model robustness, improving fairness, and enabling knowledge transfer across different data modalities.
