papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique for model compression in deep learning. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to create compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, such as mobile phones, without a significant loss in accuracy. While originally conceived for reducing model size and inference time, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now used not only for creating smaller and faster models but also for enhancing model performance, improving interpretability, and addressing practical challenges like data privacy. This demonstrates its evolution from a simple compression tool into a multifaceted framework for developing more efficient, robust, and practical artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent model compression technique to address the challenges posed by the increasing size and complexity of deep learning models. This method involves a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, more cumbersome 'teacher' model. The goal is to transfer the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the creation of compact, fast models that retain high performance. This makes state-of-the-art deep learning more accessible for deployment in resource-constrained or latency-sensitive environments, such as mobile devices. The technique has proven successful and versatile across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, such as mobile phones, without a significant loss in accuracy. The student model learns from the rich information contained in the teacher's outputs, including class probabilities and intermediate feature representations. This technique has found broad applications across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, not only for creating smaller and faster models but also for improving model robustness, generalization, and interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, especially in fields like natural language processing, have achieved state-of-the-art performance but are often too large and computationally expensive for practical deployment. Model compression techniques aim to address this challenge by creating smaller, more efficient models. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent and versatile framework for this purpose. This technique operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and replicate the knowledge of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The goal is to produce a lightweight model that retains the high performance of its larger counterpart, making it suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. This approach has proven effective across a wide range of applications, including computer vision and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning: A Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient models suitable for resource-constrained environments. The process involves a compact "student" model learning to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the rich knowledge from the teacher, the student can achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer computational resources. The applications of this paradigm extend beyond simple compression, encompassing performance enhancement, improved model robustness, and enabling learning in privacy-sensitive settings. This versatility has established knowledge distillation as a fundamental tool in natural language processing, computer vision, and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: More Than Just Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning, primarily known for model compression. It involves transferring knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, the 'student'. While the initial goal was to reduce the computational and memory footprint of models for deployment on resource-constrained devices, the application and understanding of knowledge distillation have significantly evolved. Modern approaches now leverage distillation not only for compression but also to enhance student model performance, enable training in data-scarce or private environments, and improve the robustness of learning. Advanced methods distill information from intermediate layers, attention mechanisms, and even from the student model itself in a process called self-distillation. This demonstrates that knowledge distillation is a versatile and fundamental framework for optimizing and improving deep learning models across a wide range of tasks and constraints.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for model compression in deep learning. This approach facilitates the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the teacher, to a smaller, more computationally efficient student model. The primary goal is to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. The process often involves transferring knowledge from the teacher's output distributions and intermediate features, not just the final predictions. This versatile framework has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. Advanced strategies such as multi-teacher distillation, self-distillation, and teacher-free distillation have further expanded its utility, demonstrating its importance in developing practical and efficient AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient ones. The process involves transferring knowledge from a pre-trained "teacher" model to a compact "student" model. The student is trained to mimic the teacher's outputs, such as class probabilities or internal feature representations, in addition to learning from the ground-truth data. This method leverages the rich, nuanced information captured by the teacher to improve the student's performance and generalization capabilities. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, to create lightweight models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices while maintaining high accuracy and sometimes even gaining additional benefits like improved robustness or fairness.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The primary objective is to create compact models that retain the high performance of the teacher, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. This is typically achieved by training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs or internal feature representations. While initially conceived for compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. The framework is now used to enhance student model performance, sometimes even surpassing the teacher, and to address critical considerations like algorithmic fairness and data privacy. Its versatility has led to successful applications across diverse domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, establishing it as a multifaceted tool in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a large, pre-trained model to a more compact one. This teacher-student paradigm is primarily used for model compression, enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art architectures on resource-constrained devices. However, its utility extends significantly beyond this initial purpose. The method has been successfully adapted to enhance model performance, improve generalization, and address critical concerns such as data privacy, algorithmic fairness, and model interpretability. Its flexibility across diverse domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, establishes knowledge distillation as a foundational tool for developing practical, efficient, and responsible artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Lexical Choice in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is essential for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models by reducing the complexity of the raw data with an autoregressive teacher model. In this study, we empirically show that as a side effect of this training, the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words are propagated to the NAT model from the teacher model. To alleviate this problem, we propose to expose the raw data to NAT models to restore the useful information of low-frequency words, which are missed in the distilled data. To this end, we introduce an extra Kullback-Leibler divergence term derived by comparing the lexical choice of NAT model and that embedded in the raw data. Experimental results across language pairs and model architectures demonstrate the effectiveness and universality of the proposed approach. Extensive analyses confirm our claim that our approach improves performance by reducing the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach pushes the SOTA NAT performance on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets up to 27.8 and 33.8 BLEU points, respectively. The source code will be released.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance in numerous fields, but their significant computational and memory requirements hinder their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent model compression technique to address this challenge. This method involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student model can achieve comparable performance while being significantly smaller and faster. This approach has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, with specialized techniques developed for challenges such as domain adaptation, cross-modal learning, and scenarios where original training data is unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous tasks, but their large size and computational expense often hinder their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. This method involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model, effectively transferring the teacher's learned knowledge. This process allows for the creation of compact models that are significantly faster and smaller, yet retain a high level of performance. Knowledge distillation has proven to be a flexible and effective strategy across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, enabling the development of powerful and practical AI applications.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning and natural language processing. It involves a teacher-student framework where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to transfer the rich knowledge from the complex teacher to the compact student, thereby reducing computational and storage requirements without a significant loss in performance. This allows for the deployment of powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. The process can involve transferring knowledge from the teacher's final predictions, intermediate feature representations, or attention mechanisms, and has been successfully applied across various domains, including language modeling, machine translation, and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Wright

This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a significant loss in performance. The core idea involves training the student not only on the ground-truth data but also using the outputs or intermediate representations of the trained teacher as a richer, soft target. This method has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and recommender systems, leading to a wide range of lightweight models that retain the capabilities of their larger counterparts.

papers_seen.author: Leonard

The student learns to mimic the teacher's output, thereby inheriting its capabilities. This not only enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices but can also improve the student model's accuracy and generalization ability. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition, making it a crucial tool for creating practical and efficient artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning for model compression and knowledge transfer. The core concept involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This process allows for the deployment of complex neural networks on resource-constrained devices by creating lightweight versions without a significant drop in accuracy. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation is also used to enhance model performance, transfer capabilities across different model architectures or data modalities, and address challenges such as privacy in federated learning and adversarial robustness. Its applications are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and graph-based learning.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique for model compression in deep learning. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, enabling the creation of compact models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices, without a substantial loss in performance. This approach has proven effective and versatile, with broad applications across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, for both compressing models and enhancing their overall performance.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective model compression technique that facilitates the deployment of large, complex deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, including its understanding of data structure and inter-class relationships, the student model can achieve performance far superior to what it could by training on the data alone. This approach has proven successful across various domains, including natural language processing, speech recognition, and computer vision, enabling the creation of compact models that are faster and require less memory without a significant drop in accuracy. The flexibility of knowledge distillation allows it to be combined with other techniques like data augmentation and federated learning, extending its applicability to diverse and challenging scenarios such as privacy-preservation and few-shot learning.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Transferring Inductive Biases through Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Having the right inductive biases can be crucial in many tasks or scenarios where data or computing resources are a limiting factor, or where training data is not perfectly representative of the conditions at test time. However, defining, designing and efficiently adapting inductive biases is not necessarily straightforward. In this paper, we explore the power of knowledge distillation for transferring the effect of inductive biases from one model to another. We consider families of models with different inductive biases, LSTMs vs. Transformers and CNNs vs. MLPs, in the context of tasks and scenarios where having the right inductive biases is critical. We study the effect of inductive biases on the solutions the models converge to and investigate how and to what extent the effect of inductive biases is transferred through knowledge distillation, in terms of not only performance but also different aspects of converged solutions.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: From Model Compression to a Versatile Deep Learning Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning, initially developed for model compression. It enables the creation of small, efficient "student" models by transferring knowledge from large, complex "teacher" models, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. While its primary use is to reduce computational and memory footprints, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It has evolved into a versatile framework used not only for creating compact models but also for enhancing model performance, improving interpretability, and enabling novel forms of knowledge transfer across different domains, modalities, and architectures. This demonstrates its crucial role in developing more practical, robust, and capable artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful paradigm in deep learning for compressing large, computationally expensive models into smaller, more efficient versions without a significant loss in performance. This process involves a "student" model learning to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By training on the soft probability distributions or intermediate feature representations produced by the teacher, the student model can learn richer information and achieve better generalization than if it were trained solely on hard labels. This technique extends beyond simple model compression, enabling the transfer of inductive biases, performance improvements through self-distillation, and the unification of knowledge from multiple models. Its applications are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and privacy-preserving federated learning, making it a crucial tool for deploying state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm where a compact "student" model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This process facilitates the deployment of powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by reducing their size and computational requirements. The technique has found wide application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, for tasks ranging from text generation to image classification. The core principle involves transferring the knowledge embedded in the teacher's outputs or internal representations to the student. Advanced variations of this technique have emerged, such as data-free distillation for scenarios with private data, self-distillation where a model learns from itself, and ensemble distillation using multiple teachers. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation can also be used to improve a model's performance, transfer specific capabilities like adversarial robustness, and create more efficient and generalizable models.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. This process involves transferring knowledge from a large, pre-trained "teacher" model to a smaller "student" model. The student network is trained to mimic the outputs or internal representations of the teacher, thereby inheriting its performance capabilities while having a significantly smaller footprint. This approach has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing for compressing models like BERT, as well as in computer vision for tasks such as object detection and medical image segmentation. Advanced methods have been developed to address challenges like under-fitting and to enable distillation without access to the original training data, further extending the technique's applicability and utility.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size of deep neural networks presents a significant challenge for their deployment on devices with limited computational resources. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a key model compression technique to address this issue. This method employs a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, this process enables the creation of compact and fast models that maintain high performance. The versatility of knowledge distillation has led to its successful application across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making state-of-the-art AI more practical for real-world scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm in deep learning where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of complex neural networks, enabling their deployment on resource-constrained devices without a substantial loss in performance. This is achieved by transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, such as output probabilities or internal feature representations, to the student. While initially developed for model compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly, proving its versatility across diverse domains like natural language processing and computer vision for enhancing model robustness, preserving privacy, and transferring knowledge across different model architectures.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile and Effective Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models have achieved remarkable performance but their large size and computational expense often hinder their deployment in practical, resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile model compression framework to address this challenge. This technique involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, the student can achieve comparable or even superior performance while being significantly smaller and faster. The applications of this framework are extensive, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. Moreover, advanced methods have extended its utility to scenarios where training data is unavailable and have demonstrated benefits beyond simple compression, such as improving model robustness. Knowledge distillation effectively bridges the gap between high-performance research models and practical, deployable AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale deep learning models present significant deployment challenges due to their computational and memory demands. Knowledge distillation offers a solution by transferring knowledge from a large "teacher" model to a smaller "student" model. This process trains the student to mimic the teacher's behavior, creating a compact and efficient model that retains high performance. This versatile framework enables the practical application of advanced models in resource-constrained environments across various domains like natural language processing and computer vision, and its utility extends beyond compression to areas like domain adaptation and performance enhancement.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a pivotal technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions. This process involves a teacher-student framework where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger teacher model. The primary benefit is enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, where computational power and memory are limited. The applications of this technique are widespread, spanning natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simple model size reduction, knowledge distillation is also used to enhance a model's performance, transfer beneficial properties between architectures, and improve generalization.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a prominent technique in deep learning for model compression. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to replicate the performance of a larger, more complex teacher model. The primary goal is to create smaller, faster, and more computationally efficient neural networks that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This process involves transferring knowledge from the teacher, often through its output probabilities or internal feature representations, to guide the student's training. The applications of this technique are diverse, spanning natural language processing and computer vision, and extend beyond simple compression to areas like improving model robustness, facilitating federated learning, and enhancing model performance.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Techniques such as ensembling and distillation promise model quality improvements when paired with almost any base model. However, due to increased test-time cost (for ensembles) and increased complexity of the training pipeline (for distillation), these techniques are challenging to use in industrial settings. In this paper we explore a variant of distillation which is relatively straightforward to use as it does not require a complicated multi-stage setup or many new hyperparameters. Our first claim is that online distillation enables us to use extra parallelism to fit very large datasets about twice as fast. Crucially, we can still speed up training even after we have already reached the point at which additional parallelism provides no benefit for synchronous or asynchronous stochastic gradient descent. Two neural networks trained on disjoint subsets of the data can share knowledge by encouraging each model to agree with the predictions the other model would have made. These predictions can come from a stale version of the other model so they can be safely computed using weights that only rarely get transmitted. Our second claim is that online distillation is a cost-effective way to make the exact predictions of a model dramatically more reproducible. We support our claims using experiments on the Criteo Display Ad Challenge dataset, ImageNet, and the largest to-date dataset used for neural language modeling, containing $6\times 10^{11}$ tokens and based on the Common Crawl repository of web data.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression and knowledge transfer technique in deep learning. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to replicate the performance of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in accuracy. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation can also be used to improve a model's performance, enhance its generalization capabilities across different data distributions, and transfer beneficial properties, such as inductive biases, from one model to another. The technique is versatile, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, and has given rise to numerous variations, including self-distillation, data-free distillation, and methods involving multiple or adaptive teachers.

papers_seen.author: Nunez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large, complex deep learning models into smaller, more efficient versions without a significant loss in performance. This process involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a pre-trained, high-capacity 'teacher' model. The core idea is to transfer the generalized 'dark knowledge' from the teacher's softened probability distributions or intermediate feature representations to the student. This allows the smaller model to learn more effectively than it would from hard labels alone. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition. It enables the deployment of state-of-the-art architectures on resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, and has been adapted to address challenges like data privacy, domain adaptation, and few-shot learning.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning: A Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient models suitable for resource-constrained environments. The process involves a compact "student" model learning to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the rich knowledge from the teacher, the student can achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer computational resources. The applications of this paradigm extend beyond simple compression, encompassing performance enhancement, improved model robustness, and enabling learning in privacy-sensitive settings. This versatility has established knowledge distillation as a fundamental tool in natural language processing, computer vision, and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large, complex deep learning models into smaller, more efficient counterparts. This process involves a "teacher-student" paradigm, where a smaller student network learns to mimic the outputs or internal representations of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student model can achieve comparable performance while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. This makes it possible to deploy state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, such as on mobile devices or for latency-sensitive applications. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing, where it is used to create compact language models, and computer vision, for tasks like object detection and image classification. Research continues to explore novel distillation methods, including data-free approaches and cross-architecture knowledge transfer, further enhancing its flexibility and effectiveness.
