papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework Beyond Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a foundational technique in deep learning, initially developed for model compression. This process involves training a compact 'student' model to replicate the behavior of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model, facilitating the deployment of advanced architectures in resource-constrained environments. However, the utility of this framework extends far beyond simply reducing model size. Knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile tool for enhancing model performance, transferring desirable properties such as adversarial robustness, and improving the interpretability of opaque 'black-box' models. Through advanced methods like self-distillation and applications in privacy-sensitive domains, it has become a critical component for developing more efficient, effective, and trustworthy AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Robust and Resource-Efficient Data-Free Knowledge Distillation by Generative Pseudo Replay
papers_seen.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows knowledge transfer from a trained neural network (teacher) to a more compact one (student) in the absence of original training data. Existing works use a validation set to monitor the accuracy of the student over real data and report the highest performance throughout the entire process. However, validation data may not be available at distillation time either, making it infeasible to record the student snapshot that achieved the peak accuracy. Therefore, a practical data-free KD method should be robust and ideally provide monotonically increasing student accuracy during distillation. This is challenging because the student experiences knowledge degradation due to the distribution shift of the synthetic data. A straightforward approach to overcome this issue is to store and rehearse the generated samples periodically, which increases the memory footprint and creates privacy concerns. We propose to model the distribution of the previously observed synthetic samples with a generative network. In particular, we design a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a training objective that is customized to learn the synthetic data representations optimally. The student is rehearsed by the generative pseudo replay technique, with samples produced by the VAE. Hence knowledge degradation can be prevented without storing any samples. Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that our method optimizes the expected value of the distilled model accuracy while eliminating the large memory overhead incurred by the sample-storing methods.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Transferring Inductive Biases through Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Having the right inductive biases can be crucial in many tasks or scenarios where data or computing resources are a limiting factor, or where training data is not perfectly representative of the conditions at test time. However, defining, designing and efficiently adapting inductive biases is not necessarily straightforward. In this paper, we explore the power of knowledge distillation for transferring the effect of inductive biases from one model to another. We consider families of models with different inductive biases, LSTMs vs. Transformers and CNNs vs. MLPs, in the context of tasks and scenarios where having the right inductive biases is critical. We study the effect of inductive biases on the solutions the models converge to and investigate how and to what extent the effect of inductive biases is transferred through knowledge distillation, in terms of not only performance but also different aspects of converged solutions.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Learning Student Networks via Feature Embedding
papers_seen.abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks have been widely used in numerous applications, but their demanding storage and computational resource requirements prevent their applications on mobile devices. Knowledge distillation aims to optimize a portable student network by taking the knowledge from a well-trained heavy teacher network. Traditional teacher-student based methods used to rely on additional fully-connected layers to bridge intermediate layers of teacher and student networks, which brings in a large number of auxiliary parameters. In contrast, this paper aims to propagate information from teacher to student without introducing new variables which need to be optimized. We regard the teacher-student paradigm from a new perspective of feature embedding. By introducing the locality preserving loss, the student network is encouraged to generate the low-dimensional features which could inherit intrinsic properties of their corresponding high-dimensional features from teacher network. The resulting portable network thus can naturally maintain the performance as that of the teacher network. Theoretical analysis is provided to justify the lower computation complexity of the proposed method. Experiments on benchmark datasets and well-trained networks suggest that the proposed algorithm is superior to state-of-the-art teacher-student learning methods in terms of computational and storage complexity.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm designed to create compact and efficient neural networks. This technique involves training a smaller 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring knowledge from the cumbersome teacher to the lightweight student, this approach reduces computational and memory requirements, enabling the deployment of powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, recommender systems, and graph-based learning, using a range of methods from mimicking output probabilities to distilling internal representations and employing adversarial learning frameworks.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large, state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This process involves training a smaller 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The core principle is to transfer the nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, often encapsulated in its soft predictions, to the more compact student network. This approach has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, to compress models like large language transformers and generative adversarial networks. Advanced methods have been developed that utilize multiple teachers, distill knowledge from intermediate layers, and even operate in data-free settings to address privacy concerns. Furthermore, knowledge distillation plays a crucial role in communication-efficient frameworks like federated learning, demonstrating its versatility and importance in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm where a compact "student" model is trained to reproduce the performance of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This technique addresses the challenge of deploying computationally intensive deep learning networks on resource-constrained devices. The process involves transferring knowledge from the teacher to the student, often by using the teacher's output probabilities as soft labels or by mimicking its internal feature representations. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing for tasks like machine translation and language model compression, and in computer vision for object detection and image generation. Advanced applications of this framework include enhancing model robustness, preserving privacy in federated learning, and enabling data-free model training.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved remarkable success but their large size and computational demands often prevent deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and knowledge of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers the rich, nuanced information learned by the teacher, allowing the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer resources. The utility of this technique extends beyond simple compression, with applications in enhancing model robustness, improving fairness, and enabling knowledge transfer across different data modalities. Its flexibility has led to widespread adoption in fields like natural language processing and computer vision, making it a crucial tool for developing practical and accessible AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression and Optimization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm wherein a compact "student" model is trained to reproduce the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. The primary objective is to transfer the generalized knowledge from the cumbersome teacher to the lightweight student, thereby creating a smaller, faster model suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. This technique has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. By learning from the richer, soft probability distributions output by the teacher, rather than just the hard labels from the training data, the student model can often achieve performance superior to what it could attain if trained on the data alone.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a significant loss in performance. The core idea involves training the student not only on the ground-truth data but also using the outputs or intermediate representations of the trained teacher as a richer, soft target. This method has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and recommender systems, leading to a wide range of lightweight models that retain the capabilities of their larger counterparts.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Effective Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly large-scale language models, have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous tasks. However, their significant computational and memory requirements hinder deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student model can achieve comparable performance with a fraction of the parameters and faster inference speeds. This approach has proven effective across various domains, including Natural Language Processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning, enabling the practical application of complex neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression and knowledge transfer technique in deep learning. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to replicate the performance of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in accuracy. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation can also be used to improve a model's performance, enhance its generalization capabilities across different data distributions, and transfer beneficial properties, such as inductive biases, from one model to another. The technique is versatile, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, and has given rise to numerous variations, including self-distillation, data-free distillation, and methods involving multiple or adaptive teachers.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique for model compression in deep learning. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, enabling the creation of compact models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices, without a substantial loss in performance. This approach has proven effective and versatile, with broad applications across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, for both compressing models and enhancing their overall performance.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique primarily aimed at model compression, enabling the deployment of large deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This process typically involves a smaller 'student' network learning to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' network. However, the utility of knowledge distillation extends far beyond simple compression. Its applications have expanded to include enhancing model performance on challenging tasks, enabling knowledge transfer in data-scarce or data-private scenarios, improving model fairness and interpretability, and facilitating complex learning paradigms like lifelong learning. By transferring knowledge in various forms, from output probabilities to intermediate feature representations, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile and fundamental framework for building more efficient, robust, and capable machine learning systems across diverse domains, including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models. The process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact "student" model is trained to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This enables the deployment of complex neural networks on devices with limited computational resources. Knowledge is typically transferred by training the student on the teacher's output probabilities or its internal feature representations. While its primary use is model compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness against adversarial attacks, and transferring knowledge in data-scarce or privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient ones. This process involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a pre-trained, cumbersome 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to retain the high performance of the teacher model while significantly reducing computational and storage costs, making advanced models deployable on resource-constrained devices. The applications of knowledge distillation are broad, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and healthcare. Beyond simple output matching, advanced methods focus on transferring knowledge from intermediate feature representations and using adversarial techniques to improve the student's learning process. This versatility makes knowledge distillation a crucial tool for optimizing and deploying state-of-the-art neural networks in real-world scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Tool for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning, enabling the creation of smaller, more efficient models suitable for resource-constrained environments. This process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and internal representations of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. While its primary application is to reduce computational and memory requirements without significant performance degradation, the utility of knowledge distillation has expanded considerably. It is now used to enhance model performance, transfer knowledge across different data modalities, improve model interpretability, and adapt large-scale models for specific downstream tasks in domains like natural language processing and computer vision. This versatility makes knowledge distillation a foundational strategy for developing practical and effective artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. The recent poster child of this trend is the deep language representation model, which includes BERT, ELMo, and GPT. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique for compressing large deep learning models. This method involves training a smaller, computationally efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the nuanced 'dark knowledge' from the teacher's predictions, rather than just learning from ground-truth labels, the student model can achieve performance comparable to its larger counterpart while being significantly smaller and faster. This approach has proven effective across a wide range of applications, including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices without a substantial sacrifice in accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique in deep learning for compressing large, cumbersome models into smaller, more efficient counterparts. This teacher-student learning paradigm involves training a compact student model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary goal is to transfer the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, including nuanced relationships between classes, to the student, enabling it to achieve comparable or even superior performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost. This approach has proven effective across a wide range of applications, including natural language processing and computer vision, facilitating the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices and in specialized environments like federated learning. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation also serves as a potent regularization technique and a method for enhancing model performance and enabling novel cross-modal knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful paradigm in deep learning where a compact student model is trained to reproduce the behavior of a larger, more complex teacher model. Originally conceived for model compression, this technique enables the deployment of powerful neural networks on resource-constrained devices by creating smaller, faster versions without a significant loss in performance. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation has proven to be a versatile framework with applications in domain adaptation, lifelong learning, privacy preservation, and improving the generalization capabilities of models. By transferring nuanced knowledge from the teacher, such as class relationship probabilities and internal feature representations, the student model can often achieve better performance and robustness than if it were trained on ground-truth labels alone.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique designed to train a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to emulate the performance of a larger, high-capacity 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to reduce computational and memory requirements for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in accuracy. This process involves transferring knowledge from the teacher to the student, often using the teacher's output probabilities as soft labels. Researchers have developed various methods to address challenges such as the unavailability of original training data, leading to data-free and zero-shot distillation techniques. Other advanced strategies include distilling knowledge from an ensemble of teachers into a single student, using adversarial learning to guide the process, and adapting the technique for multi-task learning and specialized domains like computer vision and natural language processing. These approaches aim to create compact models that are not only efficient but also robust and comparable in performance to their larger counterparts.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework Beyond Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a foundational technique in deep learning, initially developed for model compression. This process involves training a compact 'student' model to replicate the behavior of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model, facilitating the deployment of advanced architectures in resource-constrained environments. However, the utility of this framework extends far beyond simply reducing model size. Knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile tool for enhancing model performance, transferring desirable properties such as adversarial robustness, and improving the interpretability of opaque 'black-box' models. Through advanced methods like self-distillation and applications in privacy-sensitive domains, it has become a critical component for developing more efficient, effective, and trustworthy AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This process involves a teacher-student framework, where a compact 'student' model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The student learns from the rich, nuanced information provided by the teacher, such as its output probabilities or internal feature representations. This allows for the development of lightweight yet powerful models across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, without a significant loss in performance.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for model compression in deep learning, addressing the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models in resource-constrained environments. This method involves a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers the rich knowledge from the teacher, enabling the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer resources. Beyond simple compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include enhancing model robustness, facilitating training without original data, and improving overall performance. Its adaptability across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, highlights its role as a foundational tool for creating practical and efficient AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models have achieved unprecedented performance but their immense size and computational cost often hinder practical deployment. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression framework to address this challenge. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer resources. This makes it possible to deploy state-of-the-art models on devices with limited computational power, such as mobile phones. The technique's versatility is demonstrated by its broad application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and its adaptation into advanced methods like self-distillation and data-free distillation, further expanding its utility in developing efficient and robust AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance but are often too large and computationally expensive for practical deployment. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and inherit the knowledge of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process enables the creation of compact, fast models that retain high performance, making them suitable for resource-constrained environments. The applications of this versatile framework are broad, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition, proving essential for bridging the gap between cutting-edge research and real-world application.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary objective is to reduce the computational and memory requirements of state-of-the-art models, enabling their deployment in resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. This is achieved by training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs, which provide richer supervisory signals than traditional training labels. The technique has evolved beyond simple compression, proving to be a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, transferring knowledge across different tasks, and enabling novel applications in areas like privacy-preserving machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Dixon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique within deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient neural networks. This method operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary goal is to reduce computational and memory requirements, enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. This versatile approach has proven effective across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and its applications extend beyond simple compression to performance enhancement and knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: From Model Compression to a Versatile Deep Learning Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning, initially developed for model compression. It enables the creation of small, efficient "student" models by transferring knowledge from large, complex "teacher" models, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. While its primary use is to reduce computational and memory footprints, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It has evolved into a versatile framework used not only for creating compact models but also for enhancing model performance, improving interpretability, and enabling novel forms of knowledge transfer across different domains, modalities, and architectures. This demonstrates its crucial role in developing more practical, robust, and capable artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Paradigm for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Originally conceived as a method for a smaller "student" model to learn from a larger "teacher" model, the paradigm has evolved significantly. Research now shows that the benefits of distillation extend beyond simple mimicry, with the regularization effects of soft labels playing a crucial role. This technique has proven effective in a wide array of complex domains, including natural language processing for text generation and translation, the compression of generative adversarial networks, and the optimization of graph neural networks. Advanced methods such as self-distillation, adversarial training, and extensions for domain adaptation further highlight its versatility. Ultimately, knowledge distillation is a critical tool for creating efficient, yet powerful, AI systems suitable for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework Beyond Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning, widely recognized for its ability to compress large, complex models into smaller, more efficient "student" networks. However, its applications extend far beyond simple model compression. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is a versatile framework capable of not only creating efficient models but also enhancing their performance, enabling new functionalities, and addressing critical challenges such as fairness, privacy, and domain adaptation. By transferring knowledge from one or more "teacher" models, student models can achieve state-of-the-art results in diverse areas including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning. The evolution of distillation techniques, from mimicking output logits to advanced feature-mimicking and meta-learning approaches, further underscores its flexibility and growing importance in the development of robust and adaptable AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique for model compression in deep learning. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, enabling the creation of compact models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices, without a substantial loss in performance. This approach has proven effective and versatile, with broad applications across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, for both compressing models and enhancing their overall performance.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression, Enhancement, and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning, primarily known for model compression. This method involves training a compact "student" model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. While its main application is to create smaller, faster models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, its utility extends far beyond this initial purpose. Knowledge distillation has been successfully adapted to enhance model performance, sometimes enabling student models to surpass their teachers. Furthermore, it serves as a crucial tool for addressing important practical and ethical considerations, including improving model robustness against adversarial attacks, ensuring algorithmic fairness, preserving data privacy, and increasing model interpretability. Its flexibility allows it to be applied across diverse domains such as natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, making it a multifaceted and indispensable technique in the modern machine learning toolkit.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique for model compression in deep learning. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to create compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, such as mobile phones, without a significant loss in accuracy. While originally conceived for reducing model size and inference time, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now used not only for creating smaller and faster models but also for enhancing model performance, improving interpretability, and addressing practical challenges like data privacy. This demonstrates its evolution from a simple compression tool into a multifaceted framework for developing more efficient, robust, and practical artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.
