papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Effective Strategy for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques have emerged as a critical field of study to address these issues. Knowledge distillation, a prominent compression method, involves training a smaller 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student model to achieve performance far exceeding what it could attain by training on ground-truth labels alone. This approach has proven versatile, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, leading to models that are not only smaller and faster but also maintain high levels of accuracy, facilitating the practical application of state-of-the-art deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Effective Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly large-scale language models, have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous tasks. However, their significant computational and memory requirements hinder deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student model can achieve comparable performance with a fraction of the parameters and faster inference speeds. This approach has proven effective across various domains, including Natural Language Processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning, enabling the practical application of complex neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and powerful technique for model compression within the field of deep learning. This paradigm addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from a large 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The student is trained to mimic the behavior of the teacher, often by learning from its softened probability outputs or intermediate feature representations. This process allows the compact student model to achieve high performance, often comparable to its much larger teacher, without the associated computational and memory overhead. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated by its successful application across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making it an essential tool for developing practical and deployable AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique in deep learning for model compression and knowledge transfer. The core idea involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process allows the student to learn from the rich representations and soft probability distributions generated by the teacher, often leading to significant performance improvements over training the student model from scratch. This method is applied across a wide range of domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, to create compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a substantial loss in accuracy. Research in this area explores various distillation mechanisms, application-specific strategies, and the theoretical underpinnings of why and how this knowledge transfer is effective.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly in fields like natural language processing, have grown significantly in size and computational cost, posing challenges for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Model compression aims to create smaller, more efficient models while retaining high performance. Knowledge distillation is a prominent compression paradigm where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger 'teacher' model. This approach transfers the learned knowledge of the teacher, enabling the smaller student to achieve better performance than if trained alone. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains, with research exploring advanced techniques such as transferring knowledge from intermediate layers, using multiple teachers, and performing distillation without access to the original training data.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Enhancement in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning where a compact "student" model is trained to mimic a larger, more complex "teacher" model. The primary goal is to create smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. This is achieved by transferring the rich knowledge embedded in the teacher's outputs or internal feature representations to the student. The applications of this versatile framework are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. Beyond simply reducing model size, knowledge distillation is also used to enhance student model performance, improve generalization, and address challenges such as data privacy and algorithmic fairness.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression and knowledge transfer technique in deep learning. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to replicate the performance of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in accuracy. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation can also be used to improve a model's performance, enhance its generalization capabilities across different data distributions, and transfer beneficial properties, such as inductive biases, from one model to another. The technique is versatile, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, and has given rise to numerous variations, including self-distillation, data-free distillation, and methods involving multiple or adaptive teachers.

papers_seen.author: Patterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique that facilitates the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments by reducing computational and memory requirements without a significant loss in performance. The core idea is to train the student to mimic the behavior of the teacher, thereby inheriting its generalized understanding. This approach has proven effective across a wide array of applications in fields like natural language processing and computer vision, making it a critical tool for creating practical, real-world artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have demonstrated state-of-the-art performance but are often too large and slow for practical deployment. Knowledge distillation addresses this by training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, enabling the student to achieve comparable performance with a fraction of the computational resources. The technique has been adapted into various forms, including self-distillation where a model learns from its own past predictions and multi-teacher frameworks that leverage knowledge from an ensemble of models. Knowledge distillation is broadly applied across domains like natural language processing and computer vision to not only compress models but also to improve their interpretability, robustness, and performance on specialized tasks.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent model compression technique in deep learning, designed to address the challenges of deploying large, complex models in resource-constrained environments. The method operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, this process enables the creation of compact models that retain high performance while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. This approach has proven effective and versatile, with broad applications across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making state-of-the-art artificial intelligence more accessible for practical, real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Keith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Paradigm for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. It facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient 'student' models by transferring knowledge from larger, more complex 'teacher' models. This process enables the deployment of powerful neural networks on devices with limited computational and storage resources. The applications of this technique are widespread, moving beyond simple size reduction to include performance enhancement, improvements in model interpretability, and addressing algorithmic fairness. By leveraging the rich information captured by teacher models, distillation provides a flexible and powerful framework for optimizing deep learning systems for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Task Enhancement in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning. This method involves training a compact "student" model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. Its primary application is to create lightweight, efficient models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. The utility of knowledge distillation extends across various domains, including natural language processing for compressing large language models and computer vision for tasks like object detection and generative modeling. Advanced strategies have also been developed, such as task-adaptive compression, data-free distillation, and online learning frameworks, showcasing the versatility and ongoing evolution of this technique.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique in deep learning, primarily for model compression. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. While initially conceived to create lightweight networks suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now used to improve model robustness against adversarial attacks, transfer knowledge between different model architectures, and facilitate complex learning paradigms such as federated and continual learning. This technique has proven effective across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, demonstrating its flexibility and broad utility beyond simple compression.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly large-scale language models in Natural Language Processing (NLP), have achieved state-of-the-art performance but are often too large and slow for practical deployment. Model compression techniques are essential for creating smaller, more efficient models. Knowledge distillation is a popular compression paradigm where a compact "student" model learns from a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This process involves transferring the teacher's knowledge, often through its output probabilities or internal representations, to guide the student's training. Advanced methods have emerged, including multi-teacher distillation, self-distillation, and data-free approaches that work without the original training data. Knowledge distillation can also be combined with other compression methods like pruning and quantization to further enhance model efficiency, making powerful deep learning models accessible for resource-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique primarily aimed at model compression, enabling the deployment of large deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This process typically involves a smaller 'student' network learning to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' network. However, the utility of knowledge distillation extends far beyond simple compression. Its applications have expanded to include enhancing model performance on challenging tasks, enabling knowledge transfer in data-scarce or data-private scenarios, improving model fairness and interpretability, and facilitating complex learning paradigms like lifelong learning. By transferring knowledge in various forms, from output probabilities to intermediate feature representations, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile and fundamental framework for building more efficient, robust, and capable machine learning systems across diverse domains, including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved remarkable success but their large size and computational demands often prevent deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and knowledge of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers the rich, nuanced information learned by the teacher, allowing the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer resources. The utility of this technique extends beyond simple compression, with applications in enhancing model robustness, improving fairness, and enabling knowledge transfer across different data modalities. Its flexibility has led to widespread adoption in fields like natural language processing and computer vision, making it a crucial tool for developing practical and accessible AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Nunez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large, complex deep learning models into smaller, more efficient versions without a significant loss in performance. This process involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a pre-trained, high-capacity 'teacher' model. The core idea is to transfer the generalized 'dark knowledge' from the teacher's softened probability distributions or intermediate feature representations to the student. This allows the smaller model to learn more effectively than it would from hard labels alone. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition. It enables the deployment of state-of-the-art architectures on resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, and has been adapted to address challenges like data privacy, domain adaptation, and few-shot learning.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous domains, but their large size and computational expense often hinder deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and effective model compression technique to address this challenge. The process involves a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge embedded in the teacher's predictions or internal representations, the student can achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer parameters. The utility of this framework has expanded beyond simple compression, proving effective for enhancing model performance, transferring specific capabilities like adversarial robustness, and even mitigating societal biases within language models. Advanced methods such as self-distillation, online distillation, and data-free approaches further increase its versatility, making it a critical tool for developing efficient and practical AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for model compression, enabling the creation of smaller, more efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger, cumbersome teacher models. This process allows for the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has emerged as a versatile framework that can also enhance a model's generalization capabilities, improve its robustness against adversarial attacks, and increase its interpretability. By leveraging the rich information contained in a teacher's predictions, this technique offers a multifaceted approach to optimizing neural networks for a wide range of practical applications in natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Carney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Paradigm for Model Compression and Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning for model compression and knowledge transfer. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process allows for the creation of smaller, more efficient models that retain a significant portion of the original model's performance, making them suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Advances in this field have expanded its application beyond simple compression, with methods developed for distilling knowledge from intermediate features, ensembles of teachers, and even in scenarios where the original training data is unavailable. The versatility of knowledge distillation has led to its successful application in numerous areas, including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile and Effective Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models, while powerful, are often too large and computationally expensive for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a highly effective model compression technique to address this challenge. The process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This allows the student to learn a compressed representation of the teacher's knowledge, resulting in a compact model that retains high performance while being significantly faster and smaller. This versatility has led to its successful application across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making it an essential tool for creating practical and deployable artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for model compression in deep learning, addressing the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models in resource-constrained environments. This method involves a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers the rich knowledge from the teacher, enabling the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer resources. Beyond simple compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include enhancing model robustness, facilitating training without original data, and improving overall performance. Its adaptability across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, highlights its role as a foundational tool for creating practical and efficient AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Learning Student Networks via Feature Embedding
papers_seen.abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks have been widely used in numerous applications, but their demanding storage and computational resource requirements prevent their applications on mobile devices. Knowledge distillation aims to optimize a portable student network by taking the knowledge from a well-trained heavy teacher network. Traditional teacher-student based methods used to rely on additional fully-connected layers to bridge intermediate layers of teacher and student networks, which brings in a large number of auxiliary parameters. In contrast, this paper aims to propagate information from teacher to student without introducing new variables which need to be optimized. We regard the teacher-student paradigm from a new perspective of feature embedding. By introducing the locality preserving loss, the student network is encouraged to generate the low-dimensional features which could inherit intrinsic properties of their corresponding high-dimensional features from teacher network. The resulting portable network thus can naturally maintain the performance as that of the teacher network. Theoretical analysis is provided to justify the lower computation complexity of the proposed method. Experiments on benchmark datasets and well-trained networks suggest that the proposed algorithm is superior to state-of-the-art teacher-student learning methods in terms of computational and storage complexity.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression technique where a compact 'student' model learns to replicate the behavior of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has been shown to improve model performance, enhance interpretability, and facilitate knowledge transfer across different data modalities. However, the process is not without challenges, as student models can struggle with optimization and may inherit undesirable biases from their teachers. Ongoing research focuses on developing more effective distillation strategies, such as using multiple teachers, applying data augmentation, and mitigating fairness issues to create smaller, faster, and more robust models for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile and Effective Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models often have immense computational requirements, limiting their use in practical applications. Knowledge distillation offers a powerful solution for model compression. This technique involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process enables the creation of smaller, faster models that retain high performance, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. The versatility of this framework has led to its successful application across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, bridging the gap between state-of-the-art performance and real-world deployability.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Enhancement in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent model compression technique in deep learning and natural language processing. The method operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to create compact, high-performance models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained or latency-sensitive environments, such as mobile devices. This process allows for a significant reduction in model size and inference time while retaining the capabilities of the larger counterpart. The applications of knowledge distillation are diverse, extending beyond simple compression to include performance enhancement, knowledge transfer in privacy-preserving scenarios like federated learning, and improving model robustness across various domains.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique in deep learning, primarily for model compression. This process involves training a smaller, efficient 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, including nuanced probability distributions and internal feature representations, the student can achieve comparable or even superior performance with significantly fewer computational resources. While its primary application is creating compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, the utility of knowledge distillation extends further. It has been successfully applied to enhance model robustness, improve algorithmic fairness, facilitate domain adaptation, and increase model interpretability, making it a highly versatile and powerful tool for developing practical and efficient deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful machine learning technique focused on transferring knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the teacher, to a smaller, more efficient model, called the student. Originally conceived for model compression, this process allows for the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by creating smaller, faster versions that retain much of the original's performance. The applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly beyond simple compression. It is now used to improve the absolute performance of student models, sometimes even allowing them to outperform their teachers. Furthermore, the technique has been adapted to address challenges in diverse areas such as federated learning, data privacy, and multimodal learning. By leveraging the learned representations of a teacher, knowledge distillation provides a flexible framework for creating more practical, robust, and capable models across various domains, particularly in Natural Language Processing (NLP).

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique designed to create smaller, more efficient deep learning models. This process involves training a compact "student" model to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, this paradigm facilitates the deployment of state-of-the-art architectures in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. The technique has proven to be highly versatile, finding successful applications across a wide range of domains including natural language processing and computer vision, enabling the creation of lightweight yet powerful neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning designed to compress large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions. The process involves training a compact "student" model to mimic the behavior and outputs of a pre-trained, high-performance "teacher" model. This knowledge transfer enables the deployment of powerful artificial intelligence systems in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a substantial loss in accuracy. While originally conceived for model compression, the applications of distillation have expanded significantly, now serving as a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling advanced learning paradigms like domain adaptation and federated learning.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that addresses the challenge of deploying large, complex models in resource-constrained environments. The process involves a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This knowledge transfer allows the student to achieve high accuracy without the computational overhead of the teacher. The versatility of this framework has led to its successful application across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making it a critical tool for developing practical and accessible artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the "teacher," to a smaller, more efficient model, the "student." This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by reducing their size and inference latency without a significant loss in performance. The core idea involves training the student model to mimic the output distributions of the teacher model, effectively learning a richer, more generalized representation than it could from ground-truth labels alone. This technique has found broad applications across various domains, including Natural Language Processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. Research explores not only compressing models but also enhancing their performance, adapting them for multi-task learning, and enabling privacy-preserving or distributed learning paradigms.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of compact, efficient models from larger, more complex ones. Operating on a teacher-student paradigm, this process involves training a smaller student model to replicate the behavior of a pre-trained teacher network. The primary goal is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of state-of-the-art models, enabling their deployment on resource-constrained devices like mobile phones. The transfer of knowledge is achieved by mimicking the teacher's outputs or its internal feature representations. This versatile framework has demonstrated success across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and has evolved to address challenges such as data privacy and performance enhancement.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique in deep learning, primarily known for model compression. This process involves a teacher-student framework where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, cumbersome teacher model. The primary objective is to enable the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments by reducing computational and memory demands without a substantial loss in performance. However, the utility of knowledge distillation extends far beyond simple model compression. It has evolved into a versatile paradigm for addressing complex challenges such as domain adaptation, continual learning, and privacy preservation. By transferring knowledge in various forms, from output probabilities to intermediate feature representations, this framework enhances model efficiency, robustness, and adaptability across a wide range of applications in natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique that facilitates the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. This is achieved by training the student to mimic the outputs or internal representations of the teacher. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. Advanced methods have been developed to address specific challenges, such as transferring adversarial robustness, performing distillation without access to original training data, mitigating biases, and improving the interaction between teacher and student models.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Towards Understanding Ensemble, Knowledge Distillation and Self-Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We formally study how ensemble of deep learning models can improve test accuracy, and how the superior performance of ensemble can be distilled into a single model using knowledge distillation. We consider the challenging case where the ensemble is simply an average of the outputs of a few independently trained neural networks with the SAME architecture, trained using the SAME algorithm on the SAME data set, and they only differ by the random seeds used in the initialization.   We show that ensemble/knowledge distillation in Deep Learning works very differently from traditional learning theory (such as boosting or NTKs, neural tangent kernels). To properly understand them, we develop a theory showing that when data has a structure we refer to as ``multi-view'', then ensemble of independently trained neural networks can provably improve test accuracy, and such superior test accuracy can also be provably distilled into a single model by training a single model to match the output of the ensemble instead of the true label. Our result sheds light on how ensemble works in deep learning in a way that is completely different from traditional theorems, and how the ``dark knowledge'' is hidden in the outputs of the ensemble and can be used in distillation. In the end, we prove that self-distillation can also be viewed as implicitly combining ensemble and knowledge distillation to improve test accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile and Effective Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models have achieved remarkable performance but their large size and computational expense often hinder their deployment in practical, resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile model compression framework to address this challenge. This technique involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, the student can achieve comparable or even superior performance while being significantly smaller and faster. The applications of this framework are extensive, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. Moreover, advanced methods have extended its utility to scenarios where training data is unavailable and have demonstrated benefits beyond simple compression, such as improving model robustness. Knowledge distillation effectively bridges the gap between high-performance research models and practical, deployable AI systems.

papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models, particularly in fields like natural language processing, present significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible model compression technique to address these challenges. This approach involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, including its predictions on unlabeled data, the student model can achieve comparable performance to its larger counterpart while being significantly smaller and faster. This technique has proven effective across a wide range of applications, from compressing large language models to enabling efficient object detection and transferring knowledge across different data modalities, making it a critical tool for creating practical, real-world artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful paradigm in deep learning for compressing large, computationally expensive models into smaller, more efficient versions without a significant loss in performance. This process involves a "student" model learning to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By training on the soft probability distributions or intermediate feature representations produced by the teacher, the student model can learn richer information and achieve better generalization than if it were trained solely on hard labels. This technique extends beyond simple model compression, enabling the transfer of inductive biases, performance improvements through self-distillation, and the unification of knowledge from multiple models. Its applications are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and privacy-preserving federated learning, making it a crucial tool for deploying state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Compressing Deep Learning Models for Enhanced Efficiency
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning and natural language processing. This process allows for the deployment of powerful neural networks on devices with limited computational and storage resources, such as mobile phones. Various distillation strategies have been developed, including methods that function without access to the original training data, thereby addressing privacy and data availability concerns. By mimicking the outputs or intermediate representations of a teacher model, the student network can achieve comparable performance with a significantly smaller footprint, making it a versatile tool for optimizing deep learning applications.

By reducing computational and memory requirements, knowledge distillation facilitates the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning architectures on resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices and edge hardware. Its applications span numerous fields, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning, demonstrating its broad utility and effectiveness in making advanced AI more accessible and practical.
