papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the "teacher," to a smaller, more efficient model, the "student." This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by reducing their size and inference latency without a significant loss in performance. The core idea involves training the student model to mimic the output distributions of the teacher model, effectively learning a richer, more generalized representation than it could from ground-truth labels alone. This technique has found broad applications across various domains, including Natural Language Processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. Research explores not only compressing models but also enhancing their performance, adapting them for multi-task learning, and enabling privacy-preserving or distributed learning paradigms.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models without substantial performance degradation. The process involves transferring knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a compact 'student' model. This allows for the deployment of powerful neural networks in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. The student learns to mimic the rich output distributions and internal representations of the teacher, thereby inheriting its capabilities while maintaining a smaller footprint. This versatile framework has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and its applications extend beyond compression to areas like performance enhancement, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique for compressing large deep learning models. This method involves training a smaller, computationally efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the nuanced 'dark knowledge' from the teacher's predictions, rather than just learning from ground-truth labels, the student model can achieve performance comparable to its larger counterpart while being significantly smaller and faster. This approach has proven effective across a wide range of applications, including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices without a substantial sacrifice in accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models without substantial performance degradation. The process involves transferring knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a compact 'student' model. This allows for the deployment of powerful neural networks in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. The student learns to mimic the rich output distributions and internal representations of the teacher, thereby inheriting its capabilities while maintaining a smaller footprint. This versatile framework has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and its applications extend beyond compression to areas like performance enhancement, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, the 'student'. This process aims to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts while being significantly faster and requiring fewer computational resources. The fundamental idea is to train the student not only on the ground-truth labels but also on the soft probability distributions produced by the teacher model. This technique has been adapted in numerous ways, including transferring knowledge from intermediate layers, operating in data-free scenarios to preserve privacy, and even applying it across different tasks or data modalities. The ultimate goal is to enable the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a substantial loss in accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous tasks, but their large size and computational expense often hinder their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. This method involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model, effectively transferring the teacher's learned knowledge. This process allows for the creation of compact models that are significantly faster and smaller, yet retain a high level of performance. Knowledge distillation has proven to be a flexible and effective strategy across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, enabling the development of powerful and practical AI applications.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Technique for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique for model compression within deep learning. This process operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of complex neural networks, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. Beyond simple compression, research has shown that knowledge distillation can also enhance the performance of student models. Its applications are broad, spanning critical domains like natural language processing and computer vision, demonstrating its importance in making advanced AI systems more practical and accessible.

papers_seen.author: Velasquez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a deep learning technique primarily used for model compression, where a smaller 'student' model learns from a larger 'teacher' model. This process facilitates the deployment of powerful but cumbersome models on resource-constrained devices by reducing their computational and memory footprint. The student model is trained to mimic the teacher's outputs, effectively transferring its learned knowledge and generalization capabilities. While initially developed for creating efficient models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now used to enhance model performance, improve fairness, and enable learning in specialized contexts like federated learning and domain adaptation. The evolution of methods, such as distilling information from intermediate layers or using self-distillation, highlights its transformation into a versatile and fundamental framework for optimizing deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models, particularly large-scale language models, have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous tasks. However, their immense size and computational requirements pose significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques, especially knowledge distillation, have emerged as a powerful solution to this problem. Knowledge distillation is a process where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This allows the student to learn a compressed representation of the teacher's knowledge, resulting in a much smaller and faster model that retains a high level of performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is a highly effective and versatile framework for compressing deep learning models, enabling their practical application in diverse domains such as natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. By leveraging knowledge from a powerful but cumbersome teacher, distillation produces efficient student models that bridge the gap between high performance and practical deployability.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Robust and Resource-Efficient Data-Free Knowledge Distillation by Generative Pseudo Replay
papers_seen.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows knowledge transfer from a trained neural network (teacher) to a more compact one (student) in the absence of original training data. Existing works use a validation set to monitor the accuracy of the student over real data and report the highest performance throughout the entire process. However, validation data may not be available at distillation time either, making it infeasible to record the student snapshot that achieved the peak accuracy. Therefore, a practical data-free KD method should be robust and ideally provide monotonically increasing student accuracy during distillation. This is challenging because the student experiences knowledge degradation due to the distribution shift of the synthetic data. A straightforward approach to overcome this issue is to store and rehearse the generated samples periodically, which increases the memory footprint and creates privacy concerns. We propose to model the distribution of the previously observed synthetic samples with a generative network. In particular, we design a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a training objective that is customized to learn the synthetic data representations optimally. The student is rehearsed by the generative pseudo replay technique, with samples produced by the VAE. Hence knowledge degradation can be prevented without storing any samples. Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that our method optimizes the expected value of the distilled model accuracy while eliminating the large memory overhead incurred by the sample-storing methods.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, called the 'student'. This process enables the creation of compact neural networks that are suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. The core idea is to train the student model to mimic the output distribution of the teacher model, leveraging the rich, learned information contained in the teacher's predictions. Variations of this technique include using multiple teachers, distilling knowledge from intermediate feature layers, and even training teacher models to be more 'student-friendly'. Knowledge distillation has found wide application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, as well as in specialized paradigms like federated learning to preserve privacy and improve communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework Beyond Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning, widely recognized for its ability to compress large, complex models into smaller, more efficient "student" networks. However, its applications extend far beyond simple model compression. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is a versatile framework capable of not only creating efficient models but also enhancing their performance, enabling new functionalities, and addressing critical challenges such as fairness, privacy, and domain adaptation. By transferring knowledge from one or more "teacher" models, student models can achieve state-of-the-art results in diverse areas including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning. The evolution of distillation techniques, from mimicking output logits to advanced feature-mimicking and meta-learning approaches, further underscores its flexibility and growing importance in the development of robust and adaptable AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Beyond its primary use in creating smaller and faster models, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile framework with applications in improving model generalization, enabling knowledge transfer in data-private scenarios, and adapting models to new domains.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique in deep learning to address the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in resource-constrained environments. This process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary goal is to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making them suitable for applications on mobile devices or in latency-sensitive systems. However, the utility of knowledge distillation extends far beyond simple model compression. It serves as a powerful framework for enhancing model performance, improving robustness against adversarial attacks, and transferring complex knowledge across different architectures. Its widespread applications in natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition highlight its versatility and importance in developing practical, state-of-the-art artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Paradigm for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a versatile and powerful technique for model compression within deep learning. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process facilitates the deployment of complex, state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices by reducing their size and computational requirements. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation also serves as a method to enhance student model performance, improve generalization, and enable novel applications in areas like privacy-preserving learning and cross-modal knowledge transfer. Its flexibility has led to widespread adoption and research across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Cherry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in which a compact 'student' model is trained to emulate the performance of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of deep learning models, enabling their deployment on resource-constrained devices without a substantial loss in accuracy. This is achieved by transferring the 'knowledge' from the teacher to the student, often by using the teacher's output probabilities as soft targets for training the student. While initially focused on compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and facilitating training in privacy-sensitive or data-scarce environments. The versatility of this framework has made it a crucial tool across various domains, including computer vision and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression technique where a compact 'student' model learns to replicate the behavior of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has been shown to improve model performance, enhance interpretability, and facilitate knowledge transfer across different data modalities. However, the process is not without challenges, as student models can struggle with optimization and may inherit undesirable biases from their teachers. Ongoing research focuses on developing more effective distillation strategies, such as using multiple teachers, applying data augmentation, and mitigating fairness issues to create smaller, faster, and more robust models for real-world applications.

Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent and effective model compression technique to address this issue. The method operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve high performance with a fraction of the computational resources. Beyond its primary use in creating smaller and faster models, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile framework with applications in improving model generalization, enabling knowledge transfer in data-private scenarios, and adapting models to new domains.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient counterparts. The process involves a compact 'student' model learning to mimic the behavior of a larger 'teacher' model, enabling the deployment of powerful neural networks on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge is typically transferred by having the student replicate the teacher's output probabilities or its internal feature representations. This methodology has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile framework that can enhance model generalization, facilitate domain adaptation, and enable collaborative learning in settings like federated learning, making advanced artificial intelligence more practical and widely accessible.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique in deep learning, primarily known for model compression. This process involves a teacher-student framework where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, cumbersome teacher model. The primary objective is to enable the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments by reducing computational and memory demands without a substantial loss in performance. However, the utility of knowledge distillation extends far beyond simple model compression. It has evolved into a versatile paradigm for addressing complex challenges such as domain adaptation, continual learning, and privacy preservation. By transferring knowledge in various forms, from output probabilities to intermediate feature representations, this framework enhances model efficiency, robustness, and adaptability across a wide range of applications in natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm designed to create efficient, lightweight deep learning models. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller "student" model is trained to mimic the behavior and knowledge of a larger, more powerful "teacher" model. The primary goal is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of state-of-the-art networks, enabling their deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. Methodologies for knowledge transfer have evolved from matching output probabilities to more advanced techniques that focus on intermediate feature representations. This versatile technique has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including computer vision, natural language processing, and graph-based learning, demonstrating its effectiveness beyond simple compression to enhance overall model performance.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective model compression technique that facilitates the deployment of large, complex deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, including its understanding of data structure and inter-class relationships, the student model can achieve performance far superior to what it could by training on the data alone. This approach has proven successful across various domains, including natural language processing, speech recognition, and computer vision, enabling the creation of compact models that are faster and require less memory without a significant drop in accuracy. The flexibility of knowledge distillation allows it to be combined with other techniques like data augmentation and federated learning, extending its applicability to diverse and challenging scenarios such as privacy-preservation and few-shot learning.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of compact, efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger, more complex teacher models. This teacher-student learning paradigm enables the deployment of powerful neural networks in resource-constrained environments, such as on mobile devices, without a significant loss in performance. The process typically involves training the student to mimic the outputs or internal representations of the teacher. Beyond its primary application in creating lightweight models, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile framework used to enhance model generalization, transfer knowledge across different architectures, and enable advanced learning strategies.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly in fields like natural language processing, have grown significantly in size and computational cost, posing challenges for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Model compression aims to create smaller, more efficient models while retaining high performance. Knowledge distillation is a prominent compression paradigm where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger 'teacher' model. This approach transfers the learned knowledge of the teacher, enabling the smaller student to achieve better performance than if trained alone. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains, with research exploring advanced techniques such as transferring knowledge from intermediate layers, using multiple teachers, and performing distillation without access to the original training data.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful machine learning technique where a compact 'student' model learns from a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process enables the creation of smaller, faster, and more computationally efficient neural networks that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts. Initially conceived for model compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now widely used across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, to adapt large models for specific tasks, improve model robustness against adversarial attacks, and facilitate learning across different data modalities. By transferring learned representations rather than just final predictions, this framework provides a flexible and effective method for deploying state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for model compression in deep learning. This approach facilitates the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the teacher, to a smaller, more computationally efficient student model. The primary goal is to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. The process often involves transferring knowledge from the teacher's output distributions and intermediate features, not just the final predictions. This versatile framework has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. Advanced strategies such as multi-teacher distillation, self-distillation, and teacher-free distillation have further expanded its utility, demonstrating its importance in developing practical and efficient AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have demonstrated state-of-the-art performance but are often too large and slow for practical deployment. Knowledge distillation addresses this by training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, enabling the student to achieve comparable performance with a fraction of the computational resources. The technique has been adapted into various forms, including self-distillation where a model learns from its own past predictions and multi-teacher frameworks that leverage knowledge from an ensemble of models. Knowledge distillation is broadly applied across domains like natural language processing and computer vision to not only compress models but also to improve their interpretability, robustness, and performance on specialized tasks.

papers_seen.author: Crosby
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful and versatile model compression technique in deep learning. It employs a teacher-student framework where a smaller, computationally efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and predictions of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the nuanced knowledge from the teacher, the student can achieve comparable or even enhanced performance while having a significantly smaller footprint. This process enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices, bridging the gap between high accuracy and practical applicability in fields like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning for model compression and knowledge transfer. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to deploy high-performing models on resource-constrained devices by reducing their size and computational cost. The applications of knowledge distillation are diverse, extending from compressing large language models and generative adversarial networks to improving performance in tasks like neural machine translation, graph-based learning, and recommender systems. Variations of the technique leverage multiple teachers, adversarial samples, and feature-based mimicry to enhance the student model's capabilities, sometimes even allowing the student to surpass the performance of its teacher.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: The Versatility of Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of state-of-the-art deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques, particularly knowledge distillation, have emerged as a powerful solution. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. Knowledge distillation has proven to be a highly versatile and effective method, extending far beyond simple model size reduction for classification tasks. Its applications span diverse domains such as natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning. The framework is adaptable, enabling knowledge transfer between models of different architectures, across different data modalities, and even in scenarios with limited or no access to the original training data. This demonstrates its crucial role in making advanced AI models more practical and accessible for real-world applications.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: As deep learning models increase in size and complexity, their deployment in resource-constrained environments poses a significant challenge. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and widely adopted technique for model compression. This method involves a teacher-student learning paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student can achieve comparable or even enhanced performance with a significantly smaller computational footprint. This approach enables the practical application of state-of-the-art models on devices with limited memory and processing power, proving effective across diverse domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Hamilton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a critical technique for model compression in deep learning, addressing the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models on resource-constrained devices. This method operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student can achieve comparable accuracy with a significantly smaller footprint and faster inference times. The versatility of this approach is demonstrated by its successful application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and through the development of advanced methods like data-free and self-distillation, making it an essential tool for creating practical and efficient AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

This approach has proven effective across a wide range of applications, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, demonstrating its versatility in making advanced AI more accessible and practical.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Tool for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning, enabling the creation of smaller, more efficient models suitable for resource-constrained environments. This process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and internal representations of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. While its primary application is to reduce computational and memory requirements without significant performance degradation, the utility of knowledge distillation has expanded considerably. It is now used to enhance model performance, transfer knowledge across different data modalities, improve model interpretability, and adapt large-scale models for specific downstream tasks in domains like natural language processing and computer vision. This versatility makes knowledge distillation a foundational strategy for developing practical and effective artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large, state-of-the-art deep learning models into smaller, more efficient versions suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This process involves training a compact "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, including its predictions on unlabeled data, the student model can achieve performance far exceeding what it could by training on ground-truth labels alone. This approach has proven effective across a wide array of domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition, enabling the practical application of otherwise computationally prohibitive models. The methodology extends beyond simple output imitation, with advanced techniques focusing on transferring internal representations and adapting the teaching process itself to further enhance student performance and generalization.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex teacher model to a smaller, more efficient student model. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a significant loss in performance. This is typically achieved by training the student to mimic the outputs or internal representations of the teacher. Over time, techniques have evolved beyond simple output matching to include methods based on intermediate features, attention mechanisms, and adversarial learning. These advanced approaches have demonstrated success across a wide range of tasks and domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and generative modeling, making knowledge distillation a critical tool for operationalizing state-of-the-art deep learning models.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent technique for model compression in deep learning. This approach facilitates the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more computationally efficient model, the 'student'. The primary goal is to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. This teacher-student learning framework is not limited to simple label matching; it often involves transferring knowledge from intermediate layers and output distributions. The technique has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing for compressing large language models like BERT, and in computer vision for tasks such as object detection and image segmentation. Research has also explored advanced strategies like data-free distillation to address privacy concerns and methods to train more effective 'student-friendly' teachers.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Towards Understanding Ensemble, Knowledge Distillation and Self-Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We formally study how ensemble of deep learning models can improve test accuracy, and how the superior performance of ensemble can be distilled into a single model using knowledge distillation. We consider the challenging case where the ensemble is simply an average of the outputs of a few independently trained neural networks with the SAME architecture, trained using the SAME algorithm on the SAME data set, and they only differ by the random seeds used in the initialization.   We show that ensemble/knowledge distillation in Deep Learning works very differently from traditional learning theory (such as boosting or NTKs, neural tangent kernels). To properly understand them, we develop a theory showing that when data has a structure we refer to as ``multi-view'', then ensemble of independently trained neural networks can provably improve test accuracy, and such superior test accuracy can also be provably distilled into a single model by training a single model to match the output of the ensemble instead of the true label. Our result sheds light on how ensemble works in deep learning in a way that is completely different from traditional theorems, and how the ``dark knowledge'' is hidden in the outputs of the ensemble and can be used in distillation. In the end, we prove that self-distillation can also be viewed as implicitly combining ensemble and knowledge distillation to improve test accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.
